## `AcceleratorQuota` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuota since=v1.3}

AcceleratorQuota is one node of the fleet quota tree. Cluster-scoped: it is
fleet-level capacity policy, not a namespaced workload.


Validation: an AcceleratorQuota name may not exceed 63 characters; it is copied into a label value on every Kueue object the node materializes.

## `AutoscalerPolicy` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerPolicy since=v1.3}

AutoscalerPolicy is a reusable, parameterized autoscaler template.
Components attach individually via spec.&lt;component&gt;.autoscalerPolicyRef on
the InferenceService; the referenced template is rendered per component at
reconcile time into a verbatim ComponentAutoscaler and fed to the existing
autoscaler dispatch. Creating a policy actuates nothing by itself: the
per-component ref is the only attachment mechanism.
Alpha. The API may change without notice.

AutoscalerPolicy is off by default. To turn it on, set
`ome.autoscalerPolicy.enabled` to true on both the ome-crd and
ome-resources Helm charts, which install the CRD and its validating
webhook. The manager looks for the CRD only when it starts.

## `InferenceReplica` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplica since=v1.3}

InferenceReplica is the per-Component workload abstraction for
OMENative-managed InferenceService Components. One InferenceReplica
exists per (ISVC, Component) tuple. The ISVC controller writes the
spec; the InferenceReplica controller writes the status.

The scale subresource lets HPA/KEDA target the InferenceReplica
directly rather than indirecting through the parent ISVC.

## `TrafficMap` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMap since=v1.3}

TrafficMap is the capacity-aware routing projection of one multi-cluster
InferenceService: the per-home traffic split a gateway consumes. Placement
decides WHERE an ISVC&#39;s replicas run and quota decides HOW MUCH each home may
run; TrafficMap decides the WEIGHTS. It is generated by a control-plane
routing controller from status.placement plus accelerator-quota allocation,
never hand-edited, and consumed by a gateway-neutral publisher.
Alpha. The API may change without notice.

One TrafficMap exists per routed ISVC, named after it and owned by it (so it
is garbage-collected with the ISVC), for as long as that ISVC is routed --
including while no home is routable, when the table is empty or all-zero and
the Routable condition says why. The routing controller owns spec, SourceUID,
and the Routable, CapacityFallback, and OverrideActive conditions; the
publisher owns the rest of status, including Published and
PublicationFallback.

## Removed in v1.3 {#removed-in-v1-3}

v1.3 removes these fields. Each item says what to use instead.

- `spec.kedaConfig` on an InferenceService, and `kedaConfig` on a component. Use `autoscaler` on each component, with `class: KEDA` and a `prometheus` trigger in `keda.triggers`.
- `scaleMetric` on a component. Use `autoscaler.hpa.metrics[0].resource.name`, with `class: HPA` in `autoscaler`.
- `scaleTarget` on a component. Use `autoscaler.hpa.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization`.
- `spec.workers` on a ServingRuntime or ClusterServingRuntime. Use `spec.engineConfig.leader` and `spec.engineConfig.worker`, or the same fields on `spec.decoderConfig`.
- `status.components.<component>.latestCreatedRevision` on an InferenceService. Nothing replaces it. OMENative components report `latestReadyRevision` and `latestRolledoutRevision`.

A component is `engine`, `decoder` or `router` on an InferenceService, and `engineConfig`, `decoderConfig` or `routerConfig` on a ServingRuntime or ClusterServingRuntime.

## Supporting types

The resources above use these types in their fields.

### `AcceleratorBudget` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorBudget}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuotaSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaSpec).

AcceleratorBudget is one node&#39;s allowance of one resource on one
ResourceFlavor. Kueue quota is keyed by that pair, so both halves are needed:
a flavor names a hardware class by node labels and says nothing about which
resource the count applies to.

Accelerators are the only budgeted dimension: cpu and memory are covered on
the materialized ClusterQueue so Kueue admission never blocks on them, but
they are not authored here.

<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceName is the Kubernetes resource this allowance counts, such as
nvidia.com/gpu or google.com/tpu. It becomes the resource entry in the
materialized ClusterQueue&#39;s resourceGroup. Which names are budgetable is
operator config; the API accepts any qualified resource name.

Maximum length: `253`. Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*(/[A-Za-z0-9]([-A-Za-z0-9_.]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)?$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resourceFlavor</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceFlavor names an existing Kueue ResourceFlavor. OME references
flavors and does not own node labeling; a flavor missing on a target
cluster makes that cluster&#39;s ClusterQueue inactive, so the budget is not
materialized there.

Maximum length: `253`. Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>policy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaDistributionPolicy"><code>AcceleratorQuotaDistributionPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

Policy overrides the node&#39;s default split for this flavor only, so a leaf
can be Explicit on a reserved flavor and Proportional on a fungible one.
Leaves only.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>nominal</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Nominal is the allowance for this flavor, in the plane&#39;s own terms: the
fleet-wide total where the tree is authored, this cluster&#39;s resolved share
on a projected copy. It becomes the ClusterQueue&#39;s nominalQuota.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>borrowingLimit</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

BorrowingLimit is how far above its share this leaf may burst by borrowing
idle sibling capacity, passed through to Kueue. Unset, this leaf does not
borrow: nominal is its ceiling, and the materialized queue carries an
explicit limit of zero to say so, because the enforcement backend reads an
absent limit as unbounded.

Borrowing is cluster-local, so setting it turns nominal from a ceiling
into a floor plus overage, and the relaxed ceiling is reported in status.

WARNING: overage is not currently reclaimable. This plane sets no
preemption policy, so a borrower holds what it took until its own work
finishes -- a leaf that bursts can leave a sibling waiting for the share
that sibling was guaranteed. Leaves only.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lendingLimit</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

LendingLimit is how much of this leaf&#39;s share siblings may borrow while it
is idle, passed through to Kueue. It MUST NOT exceed the share Kueue sees.
Leaves only.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>perCluster</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorClusterShare"><code>[]AcceleratorClusterShare</code></a></td>
<td>

PerCluster is the admin-authored split, required when the effective policy
is Explicit and rejected otherwise. Entries MUST sum to Nominal. It is
absent on a projected copy, which carries one already-resolved share
rather than a fleet split.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AcceleratorBudgetStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorBudgetStatus}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuotaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaStatus).

AcceleratorBudgetStatus is one (resource, flavor) pair&#39;s resolved allowance
and observed use.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>resourceName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceName is the resource these numbers describe.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resourceFlavor</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceFlavor is the flavor these numbers describe.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>nominal</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Nominal is the resolved allowance for this plane: the fleet total where
the tree is authored, this cluster&#39;s share on a projection.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>admitted</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Admitted is the quantity of this flavor currently admitted against the
materialized queues, including anything borrowed.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reserved</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Reserved is the quantity held by workloads carrying a quota reservation,
admitted or not. It is never below Admitted, and the gap between them is
work that owns the chips but has not started — a tenant sitting at its
ceiling with Admitted low reads as idle unless this is read too.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>borrowed</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Borrowed is the admitted quantity above the nominal share, taken from idle
siblings and reclaimable on contention.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>perCluster</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorClusterBudgetStatus"><code>[]AcceleratorClusterBudgetStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

PerCluster breaks the numbers above down by cluster. Populated where the
tree is authored; empty on a projected copy, which knows only itself.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AcceleratorCapacityStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorCapacityStatus}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuotaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaStatus).

AcceleratorCapacityStatus is the observed physical capacity of one flavor, the
denominator an admin reads a budget against. It is derived, never authored.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>resourceName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceName is the resource these numbers describe.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resourceFlavor</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResourceFlavor is the flavor these numbers describe.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>allocatable</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Allocatable is the currently schedulable quantity: the flavor&#39;s resource
summed over Ready, uncordoned nodes matching the flavor&#39;s node labels.
Nodes that are NotReady or cordoned remain physical inventory but
contribute no schedulable capacity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>highWaterMark</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

HighWaterMark is the greatest Allocatable observed for this flavor. Budget
checks compare against it rather than the instantaneous value, so capacity
that shrinks — a drain, a cordon, a device-plugin restart — never marks a
node Degraded. It is lowered only once the observed value stays below it
by more than the configured hysteresis band.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

ObservedAt is when Allocatable was last sampled.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>perCluster</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorClusterCapacityStatus"><code>[]AcceleratorClusterCapacityStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

PerCluster breaks capacity down by cluster on a management plane. Empty on
a workload cluster, whose root reports only its own capacity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>attribution</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorCapacityAttribution"><code>AcceleratorCapacityAttribution</code></a></td>
<td>

Attribution identifies the hardware mapping used for this observation.
Omission cannot establish whether an observed zero is a complete sample.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AcceleratorQuotaRole` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaRole}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuotaSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaSpec).

AcceleratorQuotaRole declares what a node is, rather than leaving it inferred
from whether children happen to exist. A grouping created before its first
child is still a Cohort, and adding a child can never silently convert a leaf.

Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `Cohort`, `ClusterQueue`.

### `AcceleratorQuotaSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaSpec}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuota`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuota).

AcceleratorQuotaSpec is one node&#39;s declared position in the tree and, for a
leaf, its budget.

The rules below are same-object shape checks only. Everything needing the rest
of the tree — parent resolution, cycles, depth, containment, fleet-wide
namespace uniqueness, role transitions — is enforced by the validating webhook
at admission and re-checked by the controller at reconcile, which is the
authority. Structural checks here are also stripped from the minimal CRD
variant, so they are convenience, never the durable tier.


Validation: a ClusterQueue node must set parentRef; only the reserved root node is parent-less.

Validation: a Cohort node must not set priorityTier or distribution; no workload binds to a grouping.

Validation: a Cohort node&#39;s budgets carry only resourceName, resourceFlavor, and nominal.

Validation: a ClusterQueue node must carry at least one budget.

Validation: a budget whose effective distribution policy is Explicit must set perCluster.

Validation: a budget whose effective distribution policy is Proportional must not set perCluster; the split is computed.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>role</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaRole"><code>AcceleratorQuotaRole</code></a></td>
<td>

Role declares whether this node groups other nodes or is a leaf carrying
the budget. A node is one or the other, never both. Changing it is
admitted only under the drained-leaf / childless-grouping guard, because
the change deletes the underlying Kueue object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>parentRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaParentRef"><code>AcceleratorQuotaParentRef</code></a></td>
<td>

ParentRef is the edge to this node&#39;s parent. Every node sets it except the
single reserved root. It is mutable: re-parenting updates the materialized
ClusterQueue&#39;s cohort in place, so the queue, its LocalQueues, and its
admitted workloads all survive.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>priorityTier</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PriorityTier names the WorkloadPriorityClass stamped on this leaf&#39;s
workloads. It is a default, not a partition: a workload declaring its own
priority keeps it, and the leaf&#39;s ClusterQueue admits mixed priorities.
OME references the class and does not create it. Capped at
AcceleratorQuotaMaxNameLength because it is stamped into a label value.

Maximum length: `63`. Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>distribution</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaDistribution"><code>AcceleratorQuotaDistribution</code></a></td>
<td>

Distribution is this leaf&#39;s default split policy, overridable per budget
entry. Unset means the operator-level default from the quota config
applies; absent that too, the node reports Degraded rather than guessing.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>budgets</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorBudget"><code>[]AcceleratorBudget</code></a></td>
<td>

Budgets is the per-flavor allowance, one entry per ResourceFlavor.

On a leaf this is the budget: the fleet-wide allowance where the tree is
authored, that cluster&#39;s resolved share on a projected copy. On a Cohort
node it is an authoring guardrail only — the parent number that
parent &gt;= sum(children) is checked against. A grouping materializes as a
Kueue Cohort with no resourceGroups, so a Cohort budget is never quota
anyone can consume.

Capped at the number of entries one Kueue resourceGroup accepts.

Maximum items: `16`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AcceleratorQuotaStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaStatus}

Used by [`AcceleratorQuota`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuota).

AcceleratorQuotaStatus is the observed state of one node. The quota controller
owning the plane is its sole writer.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedGeneration is the metadata.generation the most recent status flush
reflects.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>parent</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Parent echoes the resolved parent&#39;s name, so a node&#39;s edge is readable
from status alone once the controller has confirmed it resolves.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>sourceGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

SourceGeneration is the source CR&#39;s generation this node&#39;s materialization
reflects, echoed from the projection annotation once the local controller
has materialized it. Set only on a projected copy: it is what lets the
management plane compare remote progress against what it projected, which
object-local generations cannot express.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>budgets</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorBudgetStatus"><code>[]AcceleratorBudgetStatus</code></a></td>

Budgets reports, per resource and flavor, the resolved allowance and the
usage rolled up from the materialized ClusterQueues.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>capacity</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorCapacityStatus"><code>[]AcceleratorCapacityStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Capacity is the observed accelerator capacity behind this tree, reported
on the root node only. On a management plane it is the fleet view broken
down per cluster; on a workload cluster it is that cluster&#39;s own derived
capacity, which is the only thing the local controller writes on its root.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>clusters</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaClusterStatus"><code>[]AcceleratorQuotaClusterStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Clusters reports per-cluster projection state on a management plane: which
generation each workload cluster has, and why one is behind. Empty on a
workload cluster, which projects nothing.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>materialization</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorQuotaMaterialization"><code>AcceleratorQuotaMaterialization</code></a></td>
<td>

Materialization records what this node last wrote successfully and whether
that output is currently frozen. A frozen node keeps serving its last-good
materialization; nothing is deleted while an invariant is violated.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions reports Ready, Degraded, and Materialized.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AnalysisMetric` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AnalysisMetric}

Used by [`RolloutAnalysis`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutAnalysis).

AnalysisMetric is one success condition: a PromQL query whose scalar result is
compared against Threshold with Operator. A multi-series result is reduced to
the worst series for the operator before comparison — the maximum for LT/LTE,
the minimum for GT/GTE — so the metric passes only when every series passes.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>name</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Name identifies the metric in status and events; unique within Metrics.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>query</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Query is a PromQL expression, templated with the rollout&#39;s revision context
before execution. Available variables: {{.Namespace}}, {{.ISVCName}},
{{.Component}}, {{.CanaryService}}, {{.StableService}}, {{.CanaryRevision}},
{{.StableRevision}}. A result with multiple series is reduced to the worst
series for Operator before comparison.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>operator</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComparisonOperator"><code>ComparisonOperator</code></a></td>
<td>

Operator is the comparison applied as &#34;result &lt;Operator&gt; Threshold&#34; to
decide whether this metric passes.

Allowed values: `LT`, `LTE`, `GT`, `GTE`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>threshold</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Threshold is the bound the query result is compared against. Parsed as a
float (e.g. &#34;0.05&#34;, &#34;200&#34;, &#34;1.5&#34;); admission rejects a non-numeric value.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

AnalysisMetricResult is the last observed evaluation of one AnalysisMetric.

Operator echoes the comparison that was applied.

Passed is whether this metric satisfied its condition at the last sample.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>message</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Message carries the reason when a metric did not pass or could not be
evaluated (e.g. &#34;no data&#34;, a query error).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>time</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>

Time is when this result was recorded.

<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>providerRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MetricProviderRef"><code>MetricProviderRef</code></a></td>
<td>

ProviderRef names a logical metric provider bound per cluster in the
operator&#39;s metricProviders configuration (shared with AutoscalerPolicy
triggers), which supplies the server address, auth secret, and default
headers. In a RolloutPolicy body this is the ONLY admitted spelling — a
raw cluster-local URL inside a fleet-portable object defeats
portability and is an SSRF surface. An unbound name is a deterministic
config error: the rollout parks at run open rather than starting a roll
whose gate cannot sample.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>serverAddress</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ServerAddress is the base URL of the Prometheus HTTP API
(e.g. http://prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090). Optional: when empty (and
no ProviderRef is set), the operator-configured default source
(canaryAnalysis.bundledPrometheusAddress)
is used; if that is also unset the analysis has no source and its samples read
inconclusive. Admission does not check the source — an unreachable or missing
source surfaces controller-side as an inconclusive sample, not a rejection.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>authRef</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#secretkeyselector-v1-core"><code>SecretKeySelector</code></a></td>
<td>

AuthRef points at a Secret key (in the InferenceService&#39;s namespace) holding
a bearer token sent as &#34;Authorization: Bearer &lt;token&gt;&#34;. Omit for an
unauthenticated Prometheus (the bundled one). TLS/mTLS is not supported.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>headers</code></td>
<td><code>map[string]string</code></td>
<td>

Headers are extra HTTP headers sent on every Prometheus query — e.g.
&#34;X-Scope-OrgID&#34; for a multi-tenant Cortex/Thanos/Mimir front-end that scopes
queries by tenant. Without the tenant header such a backend returns no data,
which the gate reads as a permanent stall. Plaintext (not secret); use
AuthRef for the bearer token.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AutoscalerClass` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerClass}

Used by [`AutoscalerPolicySpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerPolicySpec), [`ComponentAutoscaler`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscaler), [`ComponentAutoscalerStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscalerStatus).

AutoscalerClass identifies the autoscaler implementation for a Component.
Alpha. The API may change without notice.


Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `HPA`, `KEDA`, `External`, `None`.

### `AutoscalerManagedBy` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerManagedBy}

Used by [`ComponentAutoscalerStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscalerStatus).

AutoscalerManagedBy identifies who owns the active autoscaler for a
Component. Mirrored onto status.components.&lt;comp&gt;.autoscaler.managedBy
by the ISVC status writer so operators can tell whether OME is
reconciling the HPA / ScaledObject themselves or whether an external
operator is driving scale via the published scaleTargetRef.

none and external are STATUS-FIELD TWINS — they share the same
dispatch branch (delete any OME-managed HPA / SO and stay out) and
are distinguished ONLY here in the ManagedBy field. The status writer
inspects the resolved Class to emit &#34;external&#34; when the user opted
into a non-OME scaler vs &#34;none&#34; when scaling is disabled entirely.


Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `ome`, `external`, `none`.

### `AutoscalerPolicyProvenance` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerPolicyProvenance}

Used by [`ComponentAutoscalerStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscalerStatus).

AutoscalerPolicyProvenance reports, on the consuming InferenceService,
which policy produced a component&#39;s live autoscaler.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>name</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Name of the AutoscalerPolicy in the InferenceService&#39;s namespace.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedGeneration is the policy generation the rendered block came from.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>portableDigest</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PortableDigest is the policy&#39;s canonical spec digest — equal across
clusters iff the policy specs match.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resolvedDigest</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ResolvedDigest is a digest of the rendered ComponentAutoscaler plus the
effective bounds and bound provider endpoint. It differs per cluster by
design; its job is per-home provenance (&#34;did my policy edit land here?&#34;).

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `AutoscalerPolicyRef` {#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerPolicyRef}

Used by [`ComponentExtensionSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentExtensionSpec).

AutoscalerPolicyRef names a same-namespace AutoscalerPolicy that renders
this component&#39;s autoscaler. Deliberately a sibling of the inline
Autoscaler block, not a field inside it: ref and inline block may coexist —
the inline block wins — and that coexistence is the preview/rollback
mechanism.

<tr><td><code>kind</code></td>

Kind of the referenced policy. &#34;ClusterAutoscalerPolicy&#34; is a reserved

### `CanaryStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-CanaryStatus}

Used by [`ComponentStatusSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentStatusSpec), [`InferenceServiceStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceStatus).

CanaryStatus tracks progress of a spec.rollout.groups[].canary rollout. It is the
executor&#39;s persistent state machine: which step is active, when it was
entered (Auto promotion measures Pause.Duration from here), and which
revision is the canary. Absent when no canary is in progress.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>targetID</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

TargetID identifies the canary group&#39;s pinned Component target set. A new
target set re-arms the canary even when the externally routed Component&#39;s
revision did not change. It is scoped to the canary group rather than the
whole rollout run, so unrelated groups cannot reset canary progress.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>canaryRevisionHash</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

CanaryRevisionHash is the revision hash being rolled out.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>stableRevisionHash</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

StableRevisionHash is the revision hash that was serving as stable when
the canary began — the rollback target. It is preserved across mid-canary
retargets so a rollback always returns to the pre-canary stable revision,
never to a partially-rolled intermediate. Cleared when the canary
completes (the canary revision becomes the new stable).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>currentStep</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

CurrentStep is the zero-based index into spec.rollout.groups[i].canary.steps.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>stepEnteredTime</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

StepEnteredTime is when CurrentStep was entered. Auto promotion measures
Pause.Duration from this timestamp.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedTrafficWeight</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ObservedTrafficWeight is the external traffic weight currently programmed
for the canary revision (mirrors the active step&#39;s TrafficWeight once
applied).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>promotedThrough</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PromotedThrough is the ome.io/rollout-promote value the most recent step
advance applied. It is stamped in the same status write as the advance —
the durable record of the promotion, since metadata (the annotation) and
status cannot be written atomically. While set, a lingering annotation
with this value is inert (already applied; removal is retried
best-effort). While the rollout is in progress it clears once the
annotation is observed removed, re-arming manual promotion for later
steps.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>preStepHold</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

PreStepHold holds the canary&#39;s traffic at its currently-programmed
weight after a repin whose clamped step would raise exposure: a repin
may only hold or tighten, so the raise waits for an explicit
ome.io/rollout-promote (value = the canary revision hash). Capacity may
still converge to the clamped step — capacity ahead of traffic is the
supported warm-up pattern; only traffic and step advance hold.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rolledBackRevisionHash</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RolledBackRevisionHash is set when a rollback (ome.io/rollout-rollback)
abandons a canary: it records the primary Component&#39;s rejected revision
hash. While set, the group is held on its stable revisions and the rejected
target set is NOT retried — even after the annotation is cleared. The
rollout re-arms only when a different target set appears.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>analysisFailedChecks</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

AnalysisFailedChecks counts failing analysis samples in the CURRENT step
(reset to zero on each advance). Auto-rollback fires when it reaches
Analysis.FailureLimit. Set only under Promotion=Analysis.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastEvaluationTime</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

LastEvaluationTime is when the analysis metrics were last sampled. The
controller throttles sampling to at most once per Analysis.Interval using
this timestamp, so a burst of unrelated reconciles cannot over-count
failures. Set only under Promotion=Analysis.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastConclusiveEvaluationTime</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

LastConclusiveEvaluationTime is when analysis last produced a conclusive
sample (pass or fail — i.e. Prometheus answered). The stall timeout is
measured from here: a long run of inconclusive samples escalates to Failed.
Set only under Promotion=Analysis.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>metricResults</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AnalysisMetricResult"><code>[]AnalysisMetricResult</code></a></td>
<td>

MetricResults is the most recent per-metric evaluation, for observability
(kubectl get isvc shows why a step held or rolled back). Set only under
Promotion=Analysis.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Multiple terms form a union; a weight assigns replica shares to each match.

weight, matching term weights add and omitted weights contribute one.

<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ClusterSelectorRequirement"><code>[]ClusterSelectorRequirement</code></a></td>

<td>

MatchFields selects the real metadata.name using In or NotIn. Multiple
names are allowed; a label named metadata.name does not affect this match.

Maximum items: `64`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `ComponentAutoscalerStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscalerStatus}

Used by [`ComponentStatusSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentStatusSpec).

ComponentAutoscalerStatus reports per-Component autoscaler state on
the InferenceService. Mirrors the resolved ComponentAutoscaler block
plus the live HPA / ScaledObject metrics so an operator can read the
authoritative scaler shape, who owns it, and what it&#39;s currently
doing — all from the parent ISVC without chasing IRs and scalers
separately.

Populated by the ISVC status writer for RawDeployment- and
OMENative-managed Components.
The writer degrades gracefully when a Component has no live scaler —
ManagedBy reports &#34;none&#34; and counters stay zero without crashing.

Alpha. The shape may change without notice.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>class</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerClass"><code>AutoscalerClass</code></a></td>
<td>

Class echoes the resolved autoscaler class as picked by the
Component&#39;s deployment-mode resolver. One of HPA | KEDA | External | None.
Mirrors the input that drove dispatch so the operator can confirm
the inheritance chain landed on the expected class.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>managedBy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerManagedBy"><code>AutoscalerManagedBy</code></a></td>
<td>

ManagedBy reports who owns the underlying scaler object.
Distinguished from Class because none and external are
dispatch-equivalent (both =&gt; delete any OME-managed HPA / SO);
the surface-level distinction lives here.
  - &#34;ome&#34;: OME emitted the HPA / ScaledObject; conditions and
    replica counters below mirror its live status.
  - &#34;external&#34;: operator-owned scaler; OME publishes
    scaleTargetRef and stays out. Conditions empty.
  - &#34;none&#34;: no OME-managed scaler is active. Conditions empty;
    counters zero.

Allowed values: `ome`, `external`, `none`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>specSource</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

SpecSource reports which layer of the ISVC -&gt; policy -&gt; runtime -&gt;
legacy -&gt; default inheritance chain produced the resolved Autoscaler
block. One of &#34;isvc&#34; | &#34;policy&#34; | &#34;runtime&#34; | &#34;legacy&#34; | &#34;default&#34;.
Mirrors autoscaler.SpecSource so the operator can debug which layer is
contributing the live config.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>policy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AutoscalerPolicyProvenance"><code>AutoscalerPolicyProvenance</code></a></td>
<td>

Policy identifies the AutoscalerPolicy that rendered the live block.
Set only when SpecSource is &#34;policy&#34;.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>shadowedPolicyRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ShadowedAutoscalerPolicy"><code>ShadowedAutoscalerPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

ShadowedPolicyRef reports a policy ref outranked by an inline block
(SpecSource &#34;isvc&#34; with spec.&lt;component&gt;.autoscalerPolicyRef set). Its
wouldRenderDigest is the in-cluster preview of what the policy would
produce if the inline block were removed.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>currentReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

CurrentReplicas is mirrored from the HPA / ScaledObject status.
Zero when ManagedBy != &#34;ome&#34; or when the scaler has not yet
reported.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>desiredReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

DesiredReplicas is mirrored from the HPA / ScaledObject status.
Zero when ManagedBy != &#34;ome&#34; or when the scaler has not yet
reported.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastScaleTime</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

LastScaleTime mirrors the HPA / ScaledObject&#39;s last scale event.
Nil when ManagedBy != &#34;ome&#34;, when the scaler has not yet
reported, or when no scaling has occurred since the scaler was
created.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions mirrors the HPA&#39;s or ScaledObject&#39;s conditions
verbatim (HPA: ScalingActive / AbleToScale / ScalingLimited;
ScaledObject: Ready / Active / Fallback / Paused). Empty when
ManagedBy != &#34;ome&#34; — operator-owned scalers are surfaced via
scaleTargetRef instead.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Labels that will be added to the component pod.

<tr><td><code>minAvailable</code></td>

<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>

<tr><td><code>deploymentStrategy</code></td>

<tr><td><code>lifecycle</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleSpec"><code>LifecycleSpec</code></a></td>

Since v1.3.
Lifecycle groups OMENative-specific lifecycle policies for this
Component. Applies only when the Component resolves to deploymentMode
OMENative (spec.deploymentMode or the per-Component
ome.io/deploymentMode annotation); ignored otherwise. A field left
unset here inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value for the Component; the
controller fills what neither sets from cluster configuration and
fixed fallbacks and never writes them back. The status counterpart is

<tr><td><code>autoscaler</code></td>

underlying KEDA / HPA configuration. Takes priority over the legacy
ome.io/autoscalerClass annotation for this Component, and is the
only way to configure per-Component autoscaling: scale metrics live
here (Autoscaler.HPA.Metrics), alongside MinReplicas / MaxReplicas

<tr><td><code>autoscalerPolicyRef</code></td>

template renders this Component&#39;s autoscaler. An inline Autoscaler

without notice.

### `ComponentStatusSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentStatusSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceStatus).

ComponentStatusSpec describes the state of the component

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>url</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/knative.dev/pkg/apis#URL"><code>URL</code></a></td>

URL holds the primary url for this component.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>restURL</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/knative.dev/pkg/apis#URL"><code>URL</code></a></td>
<td>

REST endpoint of the component if available.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>address</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/knative.dev/pkg/apis/duck/v1#Addressable"><code>Addressable</code></a></td>
<td>

Addressable endpoint for the InferenceService

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>selectedAccelerator</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorSelection"><code>AcceleratorSelection</code></a></td>
<td>

SelectedAccelerator shows which AcceleratorClass was selected

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lifecycle</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleStatus"><code>LifecycleStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Lifecycle reports OMENative-managed lifecycle state for this Component
when the Component resolves to deploymentMode OMENative
(spec.deploymentMode or the per-Component ome.io/deploymentMode
annotation).
Counterpart of the LifecycleSpec sub-block on ComponentExtensionSpec.
Nil otherwise.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rolloutPhase</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPhase"><code>RolloutPhase</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
RolloutPhase reflects the current rollout state for this
Component. One of Stable, Canarying,
BlueGreenStandby, Pending, Paused, Promoting, RollingBack,
RolledBack, Failed. Empty when no rollout is in flight on this
Component (also empty for Components on deployment modes without
the rollout contract — e.g. RawDeployment).

Allowed values: `Stable`, `Canarying`, `BlueGreenStandby`, `Pending`, `Paused`, `Promoting`, `RollingBack`, `RolledBack`, `Failed`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>latestReadyRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

LatestReadyRevision is the per-revision Service name
(`<isvc>-<component>-rev-<hash>`) fronting the most recent
revision whose pods reached Ready. Equal to
LatestRolledoutRevision once the rollout completes; set ahead of
it during in-flight rollouts.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>latestRolledoutRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
LatestRolledoutRevision is the per-revision Service name
(`<isvc>-<component>-rev-<hash>`) of the most recent revision
that fully owns this Component&#39;s traffic (i.e., the rollout has
completed). Drives the consumer-side HTTPRoute backendRef.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>previousRolledoutRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
PreviousRolledoutRevision is the per-revision Service name
(`<isvc>-<component>-rev-<hash>`) of the revision that fully
owned this Component&#39;s traffic immediately before
LatestRolledoutRevision; recorded when LatestRolledoutRevision
advances. Retained for diagnosis and traffic reference during
partial rollbacks.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>traffic</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentTrafficTarget"><code>[]ComponentTrafficTarget</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Traffic reports per-revision traffic weights for this
Component. Each entry corresponds to one revision currently
receiving traffic. The HTTPRoute builder reads this to
emit weighted backendRefs.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>canary</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-CanaryStatus"><code>CanaryStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Canary tracks the canary step machine for the unit this Component
belongs to — the router alone, or engine+decoder together. It is
written on the unit&#39;s entrypoint Component (the router, or the engine)
and is absent on a secondary, so a reader never sees two copies of one
run. Absent when the unit has no canary running.

Units advance independently, which is why the state cannot live in the
single InferenceServiceStatus.Canary: two runs would overwrite each
other&#39;s step counter and revision pair. That field is retained as an
alias for the entrypoint unit&#39;s run so existing readers keep working.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>autoscaler</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscalerStatus"><code>ComponentAutoscalerStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Autoscaler reports the per-Component autoscaler state — resolved
Class / ManagedBy / SpecSource and (when ManagedBy == &#34;ome&#34;) live
CurrentReplicas / DesiredReplicas / LastScaleTime / Conditions
mirrored from the underlying HPA or ScaledObject. Populated by
the ISVC status writer for RawDeployment- and OMENative-managed
Components. See ComponentAutoscalerStatus for the full field semantics.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaleTargetRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ScaleTargetRef"><code>ScaleTargetRef</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
ScaleTargetRef is the canonical scale target for this Component.
For OMENative-managed Components this points at the
InferenceReplica&#39;s /scale subresource; for RawDeployment-managed
Components it points at the underlying Deployment. Published so
external scalers (when Autoscaler.ManagedBy == &#34;external&#34;) know
the GroupKind they should target. Populated whenever the
Component has a defined scale target — independent of whether an
OME-managed HPA / SO is active.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `ComponentTrafficTarget` {#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentTrafficTarget}

Used by [`ComponentStatusSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentStatusSpec), [`InferenceReplicaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus).

ComponentTrafficTarget describes the percentage of traffic routed to
one revision of one Component. RevisionName is the per-revision
Service name produced by OMENative&#39;s coordination layer (e.g.
`llama-engine-rev-abc123`), which the HTTPRoute builder
consumes directly as a backend reference.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>revisionName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RevisionName is the per-revision Service name for this target.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>percent</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Percent is the percentage of traffic the consumer should route
to RevisionName. Sum across all entries for one Component is
100.

Minimum: `0`. Maximum: `100`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>tag</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Tag is an optional short identifier for the target (e.g.
&#34;latest&#34;, &#34;prev&#34;). Cosmetic; not used by the consumer.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>latestRevision</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

LatestRevision is true when this entry corresponds to the
LatestRolledoutRevision for the Component.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pairingProtocol</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PairingProtocol is the engine↔decoder wire-compatibility token the
target&#39;s revision was minted under (spec.rollout.pairingProtocol at
mint time). Consumers MUST only pair engine and decoder targets whose
PairingProtocol values are equal; an empty value pairs with anything.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `DecoderSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-DecoderSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec), [`ServingRuntimeSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ServingRuntimeSpec).

DecoderSpec defines the configuration for the Decoder component (token generation in PD-disaggregated deployment).
Used specifically for prefill-decode disaggregated deployments to handle the token generation phase.
Similar to EngineSpec in structure, it allows for detailed pod and container configuration,
but is specifically used for the decode phase when separating prefill and decode processes.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><em>Embedded</em></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PodSpec"><code>PodSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

This spec provides a full PodSpec for the decoder component.
Allows complete customization of the Kubernetes Pod configuration including
containers, volumes, security contexts, affinity rules, and other pod settings.

The fields of `PodSpec` appear directly in this object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><em>Embedded</em></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentExtensionSpec"><code>ComponentExtensionSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

ComponentExtensionSpec defines deployment configuration like min/max replicas, scaling metrics, etc.
Controls scaling behavior and resource allocation for the decoder component.

The fields of `ComponentExtensionSpec` appear directly in this object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runner</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RunnerSpec"><code>RunnerSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Runner container override for customizing the main container.
This is essentially a container spec that can override the default container.
Defines the main decoder container configuration, including image,
resource requests/limits, environment variables, and command.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>leader</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LeaderSpec"><code>LeaderSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Leader node configuration (only used for multi-node deployment).
Defines the pod and container spec for the leader node that coordinates
distributed token generation in multi-node deployments.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>worker</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-WorkerSpec"><code>WorkerSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Worker nodes configuration (only used for multi-node deployment).
Defines the pod and container spec for worker nodes that perform
distributed token generation tasks as directed by the leader.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologyKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologyKey is the node-label key (e.g. an NVLink/RDMA fabric-domain label)
used to co-locate all pods of one multi-node (leader+worker) gang
into a single network / NVLink topology domain. When set on a
multi-node component, OME auto-generates the per-instance
worker→leader podAffinity that anchors every worker to its gang&#39;s
leader on a node sharing this label value — so users need not
hand-write that affinity. Only meaningful for multi-node components;
ignored for single-pod (no leader to anchor to). Unset means no
auto-generated gang affinity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpread</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TopologySpreadPolicy"><code>TopologySpreadPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologySpread spreads this component&#39;s instances across fault
domains so losing one domain (rack / fabric slice / cube) cannot
take out every instance at once. Rendered as a standard
topologySpreadConstraint (maxSkew 1) on each instance&#39;s anchor pod
(the leader, or the sole pod of a single-pod instance); workers
follow their leader, so gangs stay whole. Required renders as
DoNotSchedule — balanced spreading enforced by any scheduler that
keeps PodTopologySpread&#39;s Filter, including the OME gang
scheduler&#39;s packing profile. Preferred renders as ScheduleAnyway —
advisory only, and currently without effect under the OME gang
scheduler (its profile disables the spreading Score and pre-narrows
gang candidates to one domain). Not part of the revision hash:
changing it shapes future placements without rolling a healthy
fleet. Unset keeps pure bin-packing.

Allowed values: `Preferred`, `Required`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpreadKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologySpreadKey is the node-label key naming the fault domains
TopologySpread spreads across. Defaults to TopologyKey — right for
fabrics where the co-location domain IS the failure zone (an NVLink
rack). Set it to a coarser label when the failure zone contains many
gang domains: e.g. co-locate by the TPU partition label while
spreading across cloud.google.com/gce-topology-subblock. Single-pod
components have no co-location key, so spreading them requires
setting this explicitly. Ignored unless TopologySpread is set.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>acceleratorOverride</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorSelector"><code>AcceleratorSelector</code></a></td>
<td>

AcceleratorOverride allows overriding the global accelerator selection for this component

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `EndpointSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-EndpointSpec}

Used by [`BenchmarkJobSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-BenchmarkJobSpec).

EndpointSpec defines a reference to an inference service.
It supports either a Kubernetes-style reference (InferenceService) or an Endpoint struct for a direct URL.
Cross-namespace references are supported for InferenceService but require appropriate RBAC permissions to access resources in the target namespace.

### `EngineSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-EngineSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec), [`ServingRuntimeSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ServingRuntimeSpec).

EngineSpec defines the configuration for the Engine component (can be used for both single-node and multi-node deployments).
Provides a comprehensive specification for deploying model serving containers and pods.
It allows for complete Kubernetes pod configuration including main containers,
init containers, sidecars, volumes, and other pod-level settings.
For distributed deployments, it supports leader-worker architecture configuration.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><em>Embedded</em></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PodSpec"><code>PodSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

This spec provides a full PodSpec for the engine component.
Allows complete customization of the Kubernetes Pod configuration including
containers, volumes, security contexts, affinity rules, and other pod settings.

The fields of `PodSpec` appear directly in this object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><em>Embedded</em></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentExtensionSpec"><code>ComponentExtensionSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

ComponentExtensionSpec defines deployment configuration like min/max replicas, scaling metrics, etc.
Controls scaling behavior and resource allocation for the engine component.

The fields of `ComponentExtensionSpec` appear directly in this object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runner</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RunnerSpec"><code>RunnerSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Runner container override for customizing the engine container.
This is essentially a container spec that can override the default container.
Defines the main model runner container configuration, including image,
resource requests/limits, environment variables, and command.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>leader</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LeaderSpec"><code>LeaderSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Leader node configuration (only used for multi-node deployment).
Defines the pod and container spec for the leader node that coordinates
distributed inference in multi-node deployments.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>worker</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-WorkerSpec"><code>WorkerSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Worker nodes configuration (only used for multi-node deployment).
Defines the pod and container spec for worker nodes that perform
distributed processing tasks as directed by the leader.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologyKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologyKey is the node-label key (e.g. an NVLink/RDMA fabric-domain label)
used to co-locate all pods of one multi-node (leader+worker) gang
into a single network / NVLink topology domain. When set on a
multi-node component, OME auto-generates the per-instance
worker→leader podAffinity that anchors every worker to its gang&#39;s
leader on a node sharing this label value — so users need not
hand-write that affinity. Only meaningful for multi-node components;
ignored for single-pod (no leader to anchor to). Unset means no
auto-generated gang affinity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpread</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TopologySpreadPolicy"><code>TopologySpreadPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologySpread spreads this component&#39;s instances across fault
domains so losing one domain (rack / fabric slice / cube) cannot
take out every instance at once. Rendered as a standard
topologySpreadConstraint (maxSkew 1) on each instance&#39;s anchor pod
(the leader, or the sole pod of a single-pod instance); workers
follow their leader, so gangs stay whole. Required renders as
DoNotSchedule — balanced spreading enforced by any scheduler that
keeps PodTopologySpread&#39;s Filter, including the OME gang
scheduler&#39;s packing profile. Preferred renders as ScheduleAnyway —
advisory only, and currently without effect under the OME gang
scheduler (its profile disables the spreading Score and pre-narrows
gang candidates to one domain). Not part of the revision hash:
changing it shapes future placements without rolling a healthy
fleet. Unset keeps pure bin-packing.

Allowed values: `Preferred`, `Required`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpreadKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
TopologySpreadKey is the node-label key naming the fault domains
TopologySpread spreads across. Defaults to TopologyKey — right for
fabrics where the co-location domain IS the failure zone (an NVLink
rack). Set it to a coarser label when the failure zone contains many
gang domains: e.g. co-locate by the TPU partition label while
spreading across cloud.google.com/gce-topology-subblock. Single-pod
components have no co-location key, so spreading them requires
setting this explicitly. Ignored unless TopologySpread is set.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>acceleratorOverride</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorSelector"><code>AcceleratorSelector</code></a></td>
<td>

AcceleratorOverride allows overriding the global accelerator selection for this component

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `GroupBlueGreen` {#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupBlueGreen}

Used by [`RolloutGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup), [`RolloutPolicySpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPolicySpec).

GroupBlueGreen surges the full new set alongside the old, waits for Ready, then
flips traffic atomically. It is also the default progression a group falls back
to when none of canary/blueGreen/rollingUpdate is set. It carries no traffic
steps (the flip is all-or-nothing); surge sequencing across Components is the
group-level Order field, not a blue-green-specific knob. Empty; reserved for
blue-green-specific options (e.g. a pre-flip verification window).

### `GroupCanary` {#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupCanary}

Used by [`RolloutGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup), [`RolloutPolicySpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPolicySpec).

GroupCanary is the stepped progression: bring up new-revision capacity and
shift service-level traffic through an ordered list of steps. How the canary
advances is a PER-STEP property (see RolloutGroupStep): each step is
metric-gated (analysis), timed, manual, or immediate. Prometheus here is the
shared metrics SOURCE every analysis step queries — declared once, not on each
step.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>steps</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroupStep"><code>[]RolloutGroupStep</code></a></td>
<td>

Steps is the ordered progression of capacity + service-level traffic. The
final step must reach 100% traffic for the rollout to complete.

Maximum items: `20`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>prometheus</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AnalysisPrometheus"><code>AnalysisPrometheus</code></a></td>
<td>

Prometheus is the metrics source (connection) shared by every analysis step
in this canary: where to query and how to authenticate. When omitted (or when
its serverAddress is empty), the operator-configured default source
(canaryAnalysis.bundledPrometheusAddress) is used; if that is also unset the
analysis has no source and its samples read inconclusive. It is only the source — WHAT to
check is each step&#39;s analysis — and it gates nothing by itself.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaleDownDelaySeconds</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ScaleDownDelaySeconds is the wait between shifting traffic off the old
revision and scaling its pods down, to drain in-flight requests.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyTimeout</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

ReadyTimeout bounds how long a step&#39;s capacity gate may stay
unsatisfied before the canary is marked Failed (stable keeps serving —
no traffic has shifted). Unset falls back to the operator-configured
default (the rollout block of the operator&#39;s ConfigMap); the
ome.io/rollout-ready-timeout annotation still overrides both.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `GroupRollingUpdate` {#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupRollingUpdate}

Used by [`RolloutGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup), [`RolloutPolicySpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPolicySpec).

GroupRollingUpdate replaces pods gradually, paced by the surge/unavailable
budget. Mixed revisions are tolerated during the window.

<table class="doc-api-fields">

MaxSurge is the maximum pods (fraction or absolute) above desired during
the roll. Default 25%.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxUnavailable</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>
<td>

MaxUnavailable is the maximum pods (fraction or absolute) that may be
not-Ready at once during the roll. Default 25% (matches the Kubernetes

</td></tr>
</tbody>

### `InferenceReplicaPacing` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaPacing}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaSpec).

InferenceReplicaPacing is the per-replica projection of the active
RolloutCoordinationGroup pacing. Mirrors the corresponding
RollingUpdate subset so the projection is a verbatim
copy.

<tbody>
<tr><td><code>partition</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Partition holds back updates for Instances whose index is less
than Partition. Mirrors RollingUpdate.Partition. 0
(the default) updates all Instances. Used for canary holds.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxUnavailable</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>
<td>

MaxUnavailable caps in-rollout disruption. Accepts either a
raw count or a percent string. When nil, the InferenceReplica
controller falls back to its own default budget.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rollbackToRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RollbackToRevision, when set, names a ControllerRevision the
InferenceReplica must roll every Instance back to — overriding the
rendered desired template with that revision&#39;s stored pod template (and
using it as the update target). The InferenceService controller sets this
during a canary rollback so the forward-roll machinery drains the canary
pods back onto the stable revision. Empty in steady state.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `InferenceReplicaSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaSpec}

Used by [`InferenceReplica`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplica).

InferenceReplicaSpec is the desired state of one (ISVC, Component)
workload. The InferenceService controller is the sole writer; the
admission webhook rejects writes from other actors that lack the
ome.io/controller-write annotation.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>placementExecution</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementExecutionPolicy"><code>PlacementExecutionPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

PlacementExecution is allocation authority projected from a derived service.
Its generation must be observed before the control plane uses member evidence.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>placementReplicaLimit</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

PlacementReplicaLimit reserves the largest replica count this component
may request while placement pauses growth. Only a raised placement floor
can increase this limit; autoscaler requests remain in Replicas.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>parentRef</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ParentReference"><code>ParentReference</code></a></td>
<td>

ParentRef names the InferenceService that owns this replica.
Set by the ISVC controller at create time; immutable thereafter.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>component</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentType"><code>ComponentType</code></a></td>
<td>

Component is one of engine | decoder | router. Immutable;
moving a workload between Component slots requires recreating
the InferenceReplica.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Replicas is the desired Instance count. The HPA / KEDA scale
subresource writes this field. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>minReadySeconds</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

MinReadySeconds is the minimum time a newly Ready pod must stay
Ready before it counts as Available, projected from the parent
ISVC&#39;s spec.&lt;component&gt;.lifecycle.minReadySeconds. The workload
engine paces rollout drains and promotions on Available pods and
counts only Available pods in availableReplicas. 0 means Available
as soon as Ready.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologyKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

TopologyKey is the resolved gang co-location node-label key for this
Component, projected verbatim from the effective ISVC↔runtime
component spec (spec.&lt;component&gt;.topologyKey, else the runtime
component-config value). When set on a multi-node Component, the
InferenceReplica controller auto-generates the per-Instance
worker→leader podAffinity that co-locates every worker onto its
gang&#39;s leader on a node sharing this label value. Nil means no
auto-generated gang affinity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpread</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TopologySpreadPolicy"><code>TopologySpreadPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

TopologySpread is the resolved spreading policy for this
Component, projected verbatim from the effective ISVC↔runtime
component spec. The InferenceReplica controller renders it as a
topologySpreadConstraint on each Instance&#39;s anchor pod; nil keeps
pure bin-packing.

Allowed values: `Preferred`, `Required`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpreadKey</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

TopologySpreadKey is the resolved fault-domain node-label key
TopologySpread spreads across; nil defaults to TopologyKey.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pairingProtocol</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PairingProtocol is the engine↔decoder wire-compatibility token projected
from spec.rollout.pairingProtocol on the parent InferenceService. It is
folded into the revision hash (a change mints a new revision) and stamped
as the ome.io/pairing-protocol label on rendered pods. Projected only
onto engine and decoder — the router does not participate in P/D pairing
and must not re-roll on a protocol change. Nil pairs with anything.

Maximum length: `63`. Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9]([-A-Za-z0-9_.]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runners</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-Runner"><code>[]Runner</code></a></td>
<td>

Runners is the fully-rendered set of pod templates per Instance.
MUST be non-empty. Single-pod Instances have one Runner with
Name=&#34;default&#34; and Size=1; multi-node Instances typically have
Name=&#34;leader&#34; (Size=1) plus Name=&#34;worker&#34; (Size=N).

The InferenceService controller is the sole writer of this
field. The InferenceReplica controller treats each
Runner.Template as opaque input (same contract
appsv1.Deployment.spec.template uses).


Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lifecycle</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleSpec"><code>LifecycleSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Lifecycle holds the OMENative lifecycle policies (RestartPolicy,
UpdateStrategy, ReadyPolicy, InstanceReadyTimeout,
MigrationPolicy). Reuses the existing LifecycleSpec
type so the projection from ISVC.spec.&lt;component&gt;.lifecycle is
a verbatim copy.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pacing</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaPacing"><code>InferenceReplicaPacing</code></a></td>
<td>

Pacing is the InferenceService controller&#39;s projection of the
active RolloutCoordinationGroup pacing for this replica.
Written by the ISVC controller; read by the InferenceReplica
controller. Includes Partition (canary hold) and MaxUnavailable
(rollout budget). Nil means independent rollout.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>autoscaler</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentAutoscaler"><code>ComponentAutoscaler</code></a></td>
<td>

Autoscaler is the live autoscaler configuration that downstream
scalers (HPA / KEDA / external) target. The ISVC controller projects
the per-Component autoscaler defaults from ISVC.spec.&lt;component&gt;.autoscaler
onto the corresponding IR at create time + on subsequent reconciles.
External autoscalers may also write directly
to this field via the /scale subresource without going through the
ISVC controller.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>paused</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Paused, when true, stops the InferenceReplica controller from
initiating fleet changes: Update, Create, and Migration
operations are neither started nor advanced. The component&#39;s
RestartPolicy keeps repairing existing Instances at their current
revision unless PauseMode is Freeze. In-flight operations resume
on unpause.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pauseMode</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PauseMode"><code>PauseMode</code></a></td>
<td>

PauseMode selects how much of the lifecycle Paused suspends.
Only meaningful while Paused is true.
  - &#34;Recover&#34; (default when empty): fleet changes are suspended;
    the RestartPolicy continues to repair existing Instances at
    the revision they already run.
  - &#34;Freeze&#34;: every lifecycle operation is suspended, including
    Instance repair. Only kubelet-level container restarts and
    deliberate replica reduction (scale-down) remain active.
Status stays truthful in every depth: a Ready Instance whose pods
are all gone (and whose RestartPolicy will not repair it) is
demoted to Pending without running any recovery operation.

Allowed values: `Recover`, `Freeze`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>revisionHistoryLimit</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

RevisionHistoryLimit caps how many non-live ControllerRevisions
the InferenceReplica controller retains for this replica,
projected by the InferenceService controller from the parent
ISVC&#39;s ome.io/revision-history-limit annotation. Live revisions
(CurrentRevision / UpdateRevision and every per-Instance
running/target revision) are never deleted regardless of the
limit. Nil falls back to the operator-level
lifecycle.revisionHistoryLimit config; when that is also absent,
no revisions are pruned.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `InferenceReplicaStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus}

Used by [`InferenceReplica`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplica).

InferenceReplicaStatus is the observed state of one
InferenceReplica. The InferenceReplica controller is the sole
writer. Fields mirror the LifecycleStatus shape so the ISVC&#39;s
aggregated per-Component status is a verbatim projection of this
block.

The per-Instance rows have exactly one representation on a committed
object. Without instanceStatusEncoding the rows are the DenseV1 list
in instanceStatuses; with instanceStatusEncoding: ColumnarV2 the same
rows live in instanceStatusColumns and instanceStatuses is absent.
The rules below reject every mixed spelling of that union.


Validation: instanceStatusColumns requires instanceStatusEncoding; an unmarked status carries only instanceStatuses.

Validation: instanceStatusEncoding: ColumnarV2 requires instanceStatusColumns and forbids instanceStatuses.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedGeneration is the InferenceReplica.metadata.generation
the most recent status flush reflects.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>placementObservedGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

PlacementObservedGeneration identifies the generation reconciled with
placement rollout and replica-growth guards. The control plane requires
this acknowledgement before sharing surge allowance with the member.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Replicas is the total Instance count (any phase).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ReadyReplicas is the number of Instances whose every pod is Ready.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>servingReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ServingReplicas is the number of Instances whose every pod is
both ContainersReady AND has serving=True on the
controller-managed readiness gate (i.e., actually in the load
balancer rotation). MaxUnavailable budgets are computed
against this count, not ReadyReplicas, so &#34;missing from
traffic&#34; reflects reality during in-place updates.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>availableReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

AvailableReplicas is the number of Instances whose desired pod
count is Available: in rotation on the Component&#39;s headless
Service and, when spec.minReadySeconds is set, Ready for at least
that long.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updatedReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

UpdatedReplicas is the number of Instances on UpdateRevision.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updatedReadyReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

UpdatedReadyReplicas is the number of Instances on
UpdateRevision that are fully Ready. UpdatedReadyReplicas /
Replicas drives MaxUnavailable rollout pacing.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>currentRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

CurrentRevision names the ControllerRevision currently serving
traffic. Set by the InferenceReplica controller.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updateRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

UpdateRevision names the ControllerRevision being rolled out.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>collisionCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

CollisionCount is the salt folded into ControllerRevision hash
input after a name collision is observed, so retries produce a
different revision name. Same pattern as StatefulSet.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>labelSelector</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

LabelSelector identifies pods of this InferenceReplica for the
HPA scale subresource. Uses the same selector formula as the
Component&#39;s pod labels, so HPAs targeting either the ISVC or the
InferenceReplica resolve to the same pod set.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>instanceStatuses</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-OMENativeInstanceStatus"><code>[]OMENativeInstanceStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

InstanceStatuses is the DenseV1 representation of the per-Instance
status, one row per Instance. Absent when instanceStatusEncoding is
ColumnarV2, in which case instanceStatusColumns carries the same rows.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>instanceStatusEncoding</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusEncoding"><code>InstanceStatusEncoding</code></a></td>
<td>

InstanceStatusEncoding names the representation that carries the
per-Instance rows. Absent means DenseV1 (instanceStatuses). The only
accepted value is ColumnarV2, which requires instanceStatusColumns
and forbids instanceStatuses.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>instanceStatusColumns</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusColumns"><code>InstanceStatusColumns</code></a></td>
<td>

InstanceStatusColumns is the ColumnarV2 representation of the
per-Instance rows. Present exactly when instanceStatusEncoding is
ColumnarV2; it decodes to the same rows, in the same order, that
instanceStatuses would carry.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>retryBlocks</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RetryBlock"><code>[]RetryBlock</code></a></td>
<td>

RetryBlocks records per-target-revision retry authority for update
attempts. Revision-scoped: one block per failed target revision,
shared by every Instance attempting it — allocating a new Instance
cannot evade the block.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>migrations</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationStatus"><code>[]MigrationStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Migrations is the authoritative set of migration records for
this InferenceReplica — one entry per request UUID. Manual
entries are resumable processes born Accepted; Auto entries are
born-terminal Relocated records. Executors select on
non-terminal phase only — terminal entries are records, never
work. Non-terminal entries are never trimmed; terminal entries
are pruned once older than the migration-capacity rate window,
so the list stays bounded. Full history remains in the audit
ledger and events.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions reports InferenceReplica-level conditions. Defined
types include Available, Progressing, FailedScale,
FailedUpdate, GangSchedulingUnavailable, OperationStuck.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>traffic</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentTrafficTarget"><code>[]ComponentTrafficTarget</code></a></td>
<td>

Traffic reports per-revision traffic weights for this
InferenceReplica. Each entry corresponds to one revision
currently receiving traffic. The ISVC controller mirrors this
onto ISVC.status.components[c].traffic[] for the
HTTPRoute builder.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>coordinationGroupRef</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

CoordinationGroupRef back-references the
RolloutCoordinationGroup this replica is currently bound into
(if any). Lets operators find the owning coord group from the
child without parsing the ISVC spec.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rolloutHold</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutHold"><code>RolloutHold</code></a></td>
<td>

RolloutHold records the most recent reason a per-Instance Update was
denied for this Component — cross-Component coordination (Ratio,
Sequential), a surge/unavailability budget, or a same-target retry
hold (RetryBlock, Held). Nil while the Component is progressing or
has no rollout in flight. See RolloutHold for the field semantics.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
