### `InferenceServiceSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec}

Used by [`InferenceService`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceService).

InferenceServiceSpec is the desired state of an InferenceService.

Validation: spec.routing.capacityFactors and deprecated spec.placement.capacityFactors must not both be set.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>deploymentMode</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/ome/pkg/constants#DeploymentModeType"><code>DeploymentModeType</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
DeploymentMode selects the dispatch backend that drives every
Component on this InferenceService. When set, it propagates to
the Engine, Decoder, and Router resolver at read-time without
mutating per-Component annotations — `kubectl get -o yaml` stays
clean. A per-Component
`ome.io/deploymentMode` annotation still wins as an explicit
override (the escape hatch is preserved for backward compat and
mixed-mode experiments).

Valid values:
  - &#34;OMENative&#34;     — Native lifecycle-managed pods (also
    handles multi-node serving when Leader/Worker are present)
  - &#34;RawDeployment&#34; — Kubernetes Deployment/HPA-backed dispatch

MultiNode (LeaderWorkerSet-backed multi-node serving) is selected
via the ome.io/deploymentMode annotation or the operator-level
default, never via this field. PDDisaggregated is a shape
descriptor derived from engine+decoder pairing, and
VirtualDeployment is legacy; neither is accepted here.

Allowed values: `OMENative`, `RawDeployment`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>engine</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-EngineSpec"><code>EngineSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Engine defines the serving engine spec.
This provides detailed container and pod specifications for model serving.
It allows defining the model runner (container spec), as well as complete pod specifications
including init containers, sidecar containers, and other pod-level configurations.
Engine can also be configured for multi-node deployments using leader and worker specifications.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>decoder</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-DecoderSpec"><code>DecoderSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Decoder defines the decoder spec.
This is specifically used for PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregated serving deployments.
Similar to Engine in structure, it allows for container and pod specifications,
but is only utilized when implementing the disaggregated serving pattern
to separate the prefill and decode phases of inference.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>model</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ModelRef"><code>ModelRef</code></a></td>
<td>

Model defines the model to be used for inference, referencing either a BaseModel or a custom model.
This allows models to be managed independently of the serving configuration.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runtime</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ServingRuntimeRef"><code>ServingRuntimeRef</code></a></td>
<td>

Runtime defines the serving runtime environment that will be used to execute the model.
It is an inference service spec template that determines how the service should be deployed.
Runtime is optional - if not defined, the operator will automatically select the best runtime
based on the model&#39;s size, architecture, format, quantization, and framework.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>router</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RouterSpec"><code>RouterSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Router defines the router spec

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>acceleratorSelector</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AcceleratorSelector"><code>AcceleratorSelector</code></a></td>
<td>

AcceleratorSelector specifies accelerator selection preferences

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>traffic</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficSpec"><code>TrafficSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Traffic configures the load-balancing policy applied to all
HTTPRoutes OME emits for this InferenceService. See the
TrafficSpec doc for details.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rollout</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutSpec"><code>RolloutSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Rollout is the single home for rollout configuration on this
InferenceService: an ordered list of rollout groups, each polymorphic in
its progression (canary | blueGreen | rollingUpdate). Sequencing is the
group list order; a group&#39;s Components roll together.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scalingPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ScalingPolicy"><code>ScalingPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
ScalingPolicy coordinates replica counts across Components when more
than one autoscaler would otherwise drift (e.g., engine + decoder in
a PD-disaggregated service that requires 1:1 sharding). When nil,
every Component autoscales independently. Alpha. The API
may change without notice.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>placement</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementSpec"><code>PlacementSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Placement declares how the multi-cluster control plane selects and orders
the workload clusters this InferenceService is placed onto. When nil, the
control plane falls back to the ome.io/accelerator-requirements and
ome.io/cluster-selector annotations (unchanged legacy behavior). Only
consulted on the control-plane cluster; ignored in single-cluster
deployments. Alpha; the API may change without notice.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>routing</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingSpec"><code>RoutingSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Since v1.3.
Routing configures cross-cluster traffic distribution for this
InferenceService. Unset fields inherit the operator-level routing
configuration. Only consulted on the control-plane cluster; ignored in
single-cluster deployments. Alpha; the API may change without notice.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Statuses for the components of the InferenceService

Model related statuses

Since v1.3.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastProgressAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

LastProgressAt is when the operation last advanced. Used for stall detection.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>deadline</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

Deadline is the hard timeout for the current Step. Zero (null) means the
step clock is parked (e.g. while the instance&#39;s pods are admission-gated);
optional + nullable so the parked null is accepted by the apiserver.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>retryCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

RetryCount is the per-step escalation counter.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>targetRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

TargetRevision is the ControllerRevision the operation is converging toward.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reason</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Reason is a short cause string for the operation. Set once, when the
operation starts, by whichever state machine owns it (the restart
trigger, the revision-roll cause): it names WHY the operation
exists and must survive for the operation&#39;s lifetime.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>waiting</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Waiting is a short token naming an EXTERNAL condition currently
holding the operation back — e.g. &#34;QuotaExceeded&#34; when admission
refuses the operation&#39;s pods for lack of quota. Distinct from
Reason, which names why the operation exists: Waiting comes and
goes while the operation runs, so overloading Reason would erase
the operation&#39;s cause. Empty means nothing external is blocking.
A token only: the blocking authority&#39;s own message is volatile (an
exceeded-quota message moves as other workloads come and go) and
belongs in the Event, not in status.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>capacityRefusedAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

CapacityRefusedAt is when admission last refused one of the
operation&#39;s pod creates for lack of quota. The refusal is an
apiserver answer to a call the create pass made, so it cannot be
read off the cluster on a later pass: it is recorded here, and the
hold pass converts it into the Waiting token and the deadline park
on every pass it stands. Cleared by a create that completes with no
refusal. Empty means the last create was not refused for capacity.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>strategy</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Strategy is the update strategy the operation runs under, pinned
when the operation opens. UpdateStrategy is not part of the revision
payload, so editing it retargets nothing: an attempt keeps the
mechanism it started with — a patch already under way is not
re-dispatched as a recreate, a surge already spent is not unwound —
and the edit reaches the Instance at its next admitted attempt.
Set only when Type=Update.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>surgeIndex</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

SurgeIndex is the Instance index allocated for a surge replacement.
Set only when Type=Migrate.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>fromNode</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

FromNode is the node the migrating Instance is being moved off.
Set only when Type=Migrate.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>hintTargetNodes</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

HintTargetNodes is the caller-supplied preferred-node list for a migration.
Set only when Type=Migrate.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>requestUUID</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RequestUUID is the migration request UUID. Set only when Type=Migrate.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `InstanceStatusColumns` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusColumns}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus).

InstanceStatusColumns is the ColumnarV2 representation of the per-Instance
rows. A value shared by many Instances is stored once against the index
set of the Instances that carry it; records that are rare or unique per
Instance stay keyed by index in entries.

An index set is a string of comma-separated decimal terms, each a single
index or a closed &#34;first-last&#34; range, for example &#34;0-8,10-114,116&#34;. The
canonical form is the only accepted one: terms are strictly ascending,
disjoint, and nonadjacent (adjacent terms are merged), a range has
first &lt; last, indices are nonnegative int32 values without leading zeros,
and there is no whitespace, sign, empty term, or trailing comma.

Members is the complete row set; every other index set is a subset of it.
Within one column the group index sets are pairwise disjoint and the groups
are in canonical value order: bytewise for phases and revisions, signed
numeric for incarnations and counts. A member absent from every group of
an optional column takes that column&#39;s documented default.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>members</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Members is the index set of every Instance that has a row.

Minimum length: `1`. Pattern: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?(,(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?)*$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rowOrder</code></td>
<td><code>[]int32</code></td>
<td>

RowOrder is the dense row order when it is not the ascending Members
order: every member exactly once, in the order the DenseV1 list would
carry. Absent means ascending Members order.

Minimum items: `1`. Minimum per item: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phases</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusPhaseGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusPhaseGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

Phases groups Instances by lifecycle phase. Every member appears in
exactly one group; there is no default phase.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runningRevisions</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusRevisionGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusRevisionGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

RunningRevisions groups Instances by nonempty running revision. A
member absent from every group has an empty running revision.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>targetRevisions</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusRevisionGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusRevisionGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

TargetRevisions groups Instances by nonempty target revision. A
member absent from every group has an empty target revision.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>incarnations</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusIncarnationGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusIncarnationGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

Incarnations groups Instances by nonzero incarnation. A member absent
from every group has incarnation 0.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>podCounts</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusCountGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusCountGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

PodCounts groups Instances by positive podCount. A member absent
from every group has podCount 0.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>servingPodCounts</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusCountGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusCountGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

ServingPodCounts groups Instances by positive servingPodCount. A
member absent from every group has servingPodCount 0.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>availablePodCounts</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusCountGroup"><code>[]InstanceStatusCountGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

AvailablePodCounts groups Instances by positive availablePodCount. A
member absent from every group has availablePodCount 0.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>admitted</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Admitted is the index set of Instances whose admitted is true. Absent
means no Instance is admitted.

Minimum length: `1`. Pattern: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?(,(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?)*$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>activeOrdinalOne</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ActiveOrdinalOne is the index set of Instances whose
activeOrdinal is 1. Absent means every activeOrdinal is 0.

Minimum length: `1`. Pattern: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?(,(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?)*$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>entries</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusEntry"><code>[]InstanceStatusEntry</code></a></td>
<td>

Entries carries the per-Instance records that are not grouped:
conditions, readySince, operation, and lastFailure. At most one entry
per member, in ascending index order, each carrying at least one of
those records. A member without an entry has none of them.

Minimum items: `1`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `InstanceTermination` {#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceTermination}

Used by [`InstanceStatusEntry`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceStatusEntry), [`OMENativeInstanceStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-OMENativeInstanceStatus).

InstanceTermination captures the container-termination diagnostics of
a pod that failed or was escalated, preserved on OMENativeInstanceStatus
so the trace survives the recreate that deletes the pod.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>podName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PodName is the name of the pod that failed or was escalated.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>containerName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ContainerName is the container the diagnostics were read from.
Empty when the signal is pod-level (e.g. a pod-phase Failed with no
per-container terminated state available).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reason</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Reason is the kubelet reason for the termination or wedge — a
terminated-state reason (OOMKilled, Error, ContainerCannotRun) or a
terminal waiting-state reason (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff,
CreateContainerError). Falls back to &#34;PodFailed&#34; when only the pod
phase is available.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>exitCode</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ExitCode is the container&#39;s exit code when the diagnostics came from
a terminated state. Nil when the pod was stuck in a waiting state
(no process ever ran to produce an exit code).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>message</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Message is the kubelet-supplied detail message, if any.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>time</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

Time is when OMENative recorded this termination (reconcile time, not
the kubelet transition time, which isn&#39;t always exposed).

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MetricProviderRef"><code>MetricProviderRef</code></a></td>

### `LifecycleSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleSpec}

Used by [`ComponentExtensionSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentExtensionSpec), [`InferenceReplicaSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaSpec).

LifecycleSpec groups OMENative-specific lifecycle policies on a
Component. Embedded via ComponentExtensionSpec.Lifecycle; all fields are
no-ops unless the Component is annotated ome.io/deploymentMode=OMENative.
Nested under `lifecycle:` so the fields don't collide with corev1.PodSpec
fields (notably restartPolicy) that are also inlined into EngineSpec /
DecoderSpec / RouterSpec.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>restartPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceRestartPolicy"><code>InstanceRestartPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

RestartPolicy controls what OMENative does when a managed pod fails.
Distinct from the inlined corev1.PodSpec.RestartPolicy: that one tells
kubelet whether to restart a container in-place; this one tells the
OMENative controller whether to recreate the whole Instance. Unset
inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value; when neither sets it, multi-pod
Instances use RecreateInstanceOnPodRestart and single-pod Instances
use None.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updateStrategy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategy"><code>UpdateStrategy</code></a></td>
<td>

UpdateStrategy controls how OMENative rolls template changes across
the Component&#39;s Instances.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceReadyPolicy"><code>InstanceReadyPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

ReadyPolicy controls how Instance-level readiness is aggregated from
the underlying pods. None is accepted only for single-pod Instances,
where it is equivalent to AllPodReady; admission rejects None on
multi-pod OMENative Components because per-pod readiness reporting
is not supported. Unset inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value; when
neither sets it, multi-pod Instances use AllPodReady and single-pod
Instances use None.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>instanceReadyTimeout</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

InstanceReadyTimeout is OMENative&#39;s upper bound for waiting on a
newly-created Instance to become Ready (during migration, rollout,
or initial creation).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>minReadySeconds</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

MinReadySeconds is the minimum time a newly Ready pod must stay Ready
before OMENative treats it as Available. A pod is Available when its
PodReady condition is True and that condition&#39;s lastTransitionTime
plus MinReadySeconds is not after the current time, evaluated per pod
(the Deployment.spec.minReadySeconds rule). Ready remains the health
signal; Available is the pacing signal: a rollout drains or promotes
an Instance only once its new pods are Available, so the maxSurge /
maxUnavailable budgets stay held for the whole window, and
availableReplicas / availablePodCount count only Available pods.
Unset or 0 means Available as soon as Ready. A value authored on the
InferenceService wins; an unset value inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s;
when neither sets it, the cluster default from the
inferenceservice-config ConfigMap applies.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>migrationPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationPolicy"><code>MigrationPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

MigrationPolicy controls whether and how OMENative honors a migration
request annotation for this Component.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedGeneration is the InferenceService.metadata.generation reflected by this block.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>currentRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

CurrentRevision names the ControllerRevision currently serving traffic.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updateRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

UpdateRevision names the ControllerRevision being rolled out.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>collisionCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

CollisionCount is the salt folded into ControllerRevision hash input
after a name collision is observed, so retries produce a different
revision name. Same pattern as StatefulSet.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>labelSelector</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

LabelSelector identifies pods of this Component for HPA-style consumers.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Replicas is the total Instance count (any phase).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ReadyReplicas is the number of Instances whose every pod is Ready.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>servingReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ServingReplicas is the number of Instances whose every pod is BOTH
ContainersReady AND has serving=True on the controller-managed
readiness gate — i.e., the pod is actually in the load balancer&#39;s
rotation. This is the count operators care about for traffic
availability, and the count MaxUnavailable budgets gate against.

Diverges from ReadyReplicas during in-place updates and any other
scenario where the controller flips the serving gate to False while
containers remain technically Ready.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>availableReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

AvailableReplicas is the number of Instances whose desired pod count
is Available: in rotation on the Component&#39;s headless Service and,
when lifecycle.minReadySeconds is set, Ready for at least that long.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updatedReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

UpdatedReplicas is the number of Instances on UpdateRevision.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>updatedReadyReplicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

UpdatedReadyReplicas is the number of Instances on UpdateRevision and
fully Ready. UpdatedReadyReplicas / Replicas drives maxUnavailable
rollout pacing.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions reports Component-level conditions. Defined types include
Available, Progressing, FailedScale, FailedUpdate,
GangSchedulingUnavailable, OperationStuck.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rolloutHold</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutHold"><code>RolloutHold</code></a></td>
<td>

RolloutHold reports the most recent reason this Component&#39;s rollout
did not advance, mirrored verbatim from the owning InferenceReplica&#39;s
status. Nil while the Component is progressing or has no rollout in
flight.

</td></tr>

### `MaintainRatio` {#ome-io-v1beta1-MaintainRatio}

Used by [`RolloutGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup).

MaintainRatio bounds how far a multi-Component group may drift from the
cross-Component replica ratio observed at rollout start (e.g. prefill:decode).

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>

<td>

Tolerance is the maximum percentage drift from the starting ratio. A roll
step that would exceed it is paused until the pools rebalance. An explicit
0 means zero drift. When omitted, the operator-configured default (the
coordination block of the operator&#39;s ConfigMap) applies; if the operator
configures no default either, the group rolls with no drift bound.

Minimum: `0`. Maximum: `100`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>

### `MigrationMode` {#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationMode}

Used by [`MigrationHistoryEntry`](#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationHistoryEntry).

Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `Surge`.

### `MigrationPhase` {#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationPhase}

Used by [`MigrationHistoryEntry`](#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationHistoryEntry), [`MigrationStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationStatus).

MigrationPhase is the lifecycle phase of a migration.

Manual migrations walk Accepted -&gt; SurgePending -&gt; SurgeReady -&gt;
Draining -&gt; Completed | Failed. Auto relocations are born terminal
(Relocated). Terminal phases are Completed, Failed, and Relocated —
executors select work on non-terminal phase only; terminal entries
are records, never work.

Pending and InProgress are legacy values used only by the ISVC
status migrationHistory window.

Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `Accepted`, `SurgePending`, `SurgeReady`, `Draining`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Relocated`, `Pending`, `InProgress`.

### `MigrationPolicy` {#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationPolicy}

Used by [`LifecycleSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleSpec).

MigrationPolicy controls whether and how OMENative honors migration requests
(both automatic deadline-disposition relocation and explicit annotation-triggered migration).

<td>

Mode gates migration: Auto enables both deadline-disposition relocation and
explicit migration requests; Never disables both. Unset inherits the
ServingRuntime&#39;s value, then Auto.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Allowed values: `Auto`, `Surge`, `Never`.

### `MigrationStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationStatus}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus).

MigrationStatus is one migration request&#39;s authoritative record on
the InferenceReplica. status.migrations is the single source of
truth for migration work: executors resume from non-terminal
entries; the audit ledger and events are history, not work.

Lifecycle contract:
  - Manual entries (Trigger=Manual) are resumable processes: born
    Accepted, they walk Accepted -&gt; SurgePending -&gt; SurgeReady -&gt;
    Draining -&gt; Completed | Failed.
  - Auto entries (Trigger=Auto) are born-terminal Relocated records
    mirroring a relocation directive; Succeeded is stamped post-hoc
    when the relocated Instance next reaches Ready.
  - Executors select on non-terminal phase only — terminal entries
    are records, never work.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>requestUUID</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RequestUUID uniquely identifies the migration request. Manual:
supplied by the requester. Auto: generated by the controller.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>trigger</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationTrigger"><code>MigrationTrigger</code></a></td>
<td>

Trigger records who initiated the migration.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>sourceInstance</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

SourceInstance is the Instance index being migrated away from.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>surgeInstance</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

SurgeInstance is the Instance index allocated for the surge
replacement. Manual only; nil until allocated. Distinct from
index 0, which is a valid surge index.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>allocatedAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

AllocatedAt is when the surge Instance index was allocated —
the start of execution. Nil while the entry is queued (Accepted
but not yet picked up by the executor). The capacity gate counts
execution from this stamp, never queued intent.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>fromNode</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

FromNode is the node the source is being moved off.
Auto: the excluded node.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>hintTargetNodes</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

HintTargetNodes are requester-supplied preferred placement
targets for the surge replacement. Rendered as preferred (soft)
node affinity; the scheduler may pick other nodes.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phase</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MigrationPhase"><code>MigrationPhase</code></a></td>
<td>

Phase is the migration lifecycle phase. See MigrationPhase for
the Manual chain, the Auto born-terminal rule, and the terminal
set.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>attempt</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Attempt is the relocation attempt ordinal.
Auto: N of autoMigrate.maxAttempts.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reason</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Reason is the requester-supplied reason (Manual) or the
disposition branch that produced the entry (Auto).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>message</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Message describes the current blocker (non-terminal) or the
terminal outcome.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>startedAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

StartedAt is when the entry was created.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>deadline</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

Deadline is when a non-terminal entry expires.
Manual: accept time plus InstanceReadyTimeout.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>completedAt</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

CompletedAt is when the entry reached a terminal phase.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>succeeded</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Succeeded reports the post-hoc outcome. Auto: stamped true when
the relocated Instance next reaches Ready.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `OMENativeInstanceStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-OMENativeInstanceStatus}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus).

OMENativeInstanceStatus reports state for one OMENative Instance.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>index</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Index is the stable Instance ordinal. Values may be sparse after surge migration.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>incarnation</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

Incarnation increments each time the Instance is recreated (full
recreate update, restart-on-loss). In-place updates do not increment.
Stamped on pods via the `ome.io/instance-incarnation` label.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phase</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-OMENativeInstancePhase"><code>OMENativeInstancePhase</code></a></td>
<td>

Phase is the lifecycle phase of the Instance.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runningRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

RunningRevision is the ControllerRevision the live pods are running.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>targetRevision</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

TargetRevision is the ControllerRevision the live pods are converging toward.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>podCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

PodCount is the total number of pods owned by this Instance.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyPodCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ReadyPodCount is retained for API compatibility. OMENative derives
readiness from Pods and does not persist this field.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>servingPodCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ServingPodCount is the number of pods that are BOTH ContainersReady
AND have serving=True on the controller-managed readiness gate —
i.e., pods actually in the load balancer rotation. Diverges from
ReadyPodCount whenever the controller flips the serving gate
(in-place updates, drain steps, etc.). MaxUnavailable budgets are
computed against the serving count, not the ready count, so that
&#34;missing from traffic&#34; reflects reality.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>availablePodCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

AvailablePodCount is the number of pods that are Available: in
rotation on the Component&#39;s headless Service and, when
lifecycle.minReadySeconds is set, Ready for at least that long.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduledPodCount</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ScheduledPodCount is retained for API compatibility. OMENative derives
scheduling state from Pods and does not persist this field.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>admitted</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Admitted is true when this Instance&#39;s pods have left the Kueue admission
scheduling gate (quota granted): the Instance has pods and none are
admission-gated. False while gated/queued or before pods exist. Used by
the control plane to decide the fan-out race winner.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>nodesOccupied</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

NodesOccupied is retained for API compatibility. OMENative reads current
placement from Pods and does not persist this field.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions reports Instance-level conditions. Defined types include
AllPodsScheduled, AllPodsReady, AllPodsAvailable, Drained, Failed,
ProgressDeadlineExceeded.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readySince</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

ReadySince is when the Instance last entered Ready. Anchors
post-Ready failure detection: container restarts that finished
before this time belong to boot and never trigger a recreate.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>operation</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceOperation"><code>InstanceOperation</code></a></td>
<td>

Operation is the durable record of an in-flight destructive action
against this Instance. Set before the action starts, cleared after
it completes. Lets a crashed controller resume work without diffing
pod state.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>activeOrdinal</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ActiveOrdinal identifies which of two pod-naming slots
(0 or 1) currently holds the canonical pod for this single-pod
Instance. SurgeThenDrain alternates between slots: the surge
creates a new pod at `1 - ActiveOrdinal`, waits Ready, drains
the old pod, then advances ActiveOrdinal to the new slot. Stays
0 for InPlace and Recreate strategies (those reuse the same
pod name). Defaults to 0 on initial create.

Minimum: `0`. Maximum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastFailure</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InstanceTermination"><code>InstanceTermination</code></a></td>
<td>

LastFailure preserves the diagnostics of the pod whose failure
(or stuck-pod escalation) last triggered a recreate of this
Instance. OMENative drains and deletes every gang pod on recreate,
so the failing pod and its container termination state vanish from
the cluster — this field is the surviving trace operators read when
a multi-node Instance keeps recreating. Set on the first pass of a
failure-driven Restart and on stuck-pod escalation; left untouched
by revision-roll recreates (those carry their cause in
Operation.Reason instead) so the most recent genuine failure isn&#39;t
overwritten by a clean rollout.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>announced</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

Announced records the once-only messages this Instance has already
emitted, one entry per message: the event reason it was emitted
under and the episode it was emitted in, joined by &#34;@&#34;. A warning
an operator needs to see once — the gang has no co-location term,
the PodGroup was rebuilt, a repair is held, a drain is past its
deadline — is emitted only when its entry is absent, and is
stamped in the same write that emits it. Recording it on the
Instance rather than in controller memory is what makes the
once-only property hold per workload rather than per process, and
survive a controller restart.

The episode is the in-flight operation, or the incarnation when
there is none: a new attempt or a rebuilt Instance has its own
messages to deliver, and the entries of the episode it replaced no
longer match.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `PlacementSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec).

PlacementSpec declares how the control plane selects the workload clusters an
InferenceService is placed onto, and how many of them serve it. It subsumes the
legacy ome.io/accelerator-requirements and ome.io/cluster-selector annotations
in a typed, schema-validated form; when this field is nil the control plane
still honors those annotations for backward compatibility.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>mode</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementMode"><code>PlacementMode</code></a></td>
<td>

Mode is the placement cardinality: Single (one cluster), All (every
candidate), or Split (replicas distributed across clusters). Defaults to
Single. All and Split are rejected by admission on a control plane that
does not implement them.

Default: `Single`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>requirements</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Requirements is the intrinsic capability selector a candidate workload
cluster MUST satisfy, expressed as a Kubernetes label-selector string
matched against WorkloadCluster labels plus the virtual, immutable
metadata.name key (e.g. &#34;accelerator in (gb300, tpu7x)&#34;). It is the
structured equivalent of the ome.io/accelerator-requirements annotation.
Empty means no intrinsic requirement.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>clusterSelector</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ClusterSelector is an optional operator-imposed routing overlay
(label-selector string) AND-ed onto Requirements to further narrow
candidates. It can select WorkloadCluster labels (e.g. &#34;provider=cloud-a&#34;)
or immutable object names (e.g. &#34;metadata.name in (cluster-a,cluster-c)&#34;).
Structured equivalent of the ome.io/cluster-selector annotation.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>split</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-SplitSpec"><code>SplitSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Split tunes Split mode (distributing replicas across clusters). Only
consulted when Mode is Split; ignored otherwise. Nil means Split defaults:
distribute the engine&#39;s minReplicas, packed onto the fewest clusters.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>capacityFactors</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>map[string]Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

CapacityFactors overrides the per-replica relative serving capacity of
named workload clusters, keyed by WorkloadCluster name. It weights traffic
for heterogeneous hardware where one cluster&#39;s replica serves more (or less)
than another&#39;s: a home&#39;s routed share scales with its admitted replicas
times this factor. A quantity of &#34;2&#34; means each replica on that cluster
carries twice the share of a factor-1 replica; &#34;500m&#34; means half. A cluster
absent from the map (or the whole field unset) uses the identity factor 1.
This is a routing weight only — it does not influence placement or how many
replicas a cluster admits.

Deprecated: use spec.routing.capacityFactors.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Endpoint is the externally-addressable URL of the winning cluster in Single

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>candidates</code></td>

<td>

Candidates are the clusters this ISVC has been fanned out to during
placement. Populated by the control plane.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Init containers may not have Lifecycle actions, Readiness probes, Liveness probes, or Startup probes.

The RuntimeClass admission controller will reject Pod create requests which have the overhead already
set. If RuntimeClass is configured and selected in the PodSpec, Overhead will be set to the value
defined in the corresponding RuntimeClass, otherwise it will remain unset and treated as zero.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/688-pod-overhead/README.md

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>topologySpreadConstraints</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#topologyspreadconstraint-v1-core"><code>[]TopologySpreadConstraint</code></a></td>
<td>

TopologySpreadConstraints describes how a group of pods ought to spread across topology
domains. Scheduler will schedule pods in a way which abides by the constraints.
All topologySpreadConstraints are ANDed.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>setHostnameAsFQDN</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

If true the pod&#39;s hostname will be configured as the pod&#39;s FQDN, rather than the leaf name (the default).
In Linux containers, this means setting the FQDN in the hostname field of the kernel (the nodename field of struct utsname).
In Windows containers, this means setting the registry value of hostname for the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\Tcpip\\Parameters to FQDN.
If a pod does not have FQDN, this has no effect.
Default to false.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>os</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#podos-v1-core"><code>PodOS</code></a></td>
<td>

Specifies the OS of the containers in the pod.
Some pod and container fields are restricted if this is set.

If the OS field is set to linux, the following fields must be unset:
-securityContext.windowsOptions

If the OS field is set to windows, following fields must be unset:
- spec.hostPID
- spec.hostIPC
- spec.hostUsers
- spec.securityContext.appArmorProfile
- spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions
- spec.securityContext.seccompProfile
- spec.securityContext.fsGroup
- spec.securityContext.fsGroupChangePolicy
- spec.securityContext.sysctls
- spec.shareProcessNamespace
- spec.securityContext.runAsUser
- spec.securityContext.runAsGroup
- spec.securityContext.supplementalGroups
- spec.securityContext.supplementalGroupsPolicy
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.appArmorProfile
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.seLinuxOptions
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.seccompProfile
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.privileged
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.procMount
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsUser
- spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsGroup

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>hostUsers</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Use the host&#39;s user namespace.
Optional: Default to true.
If set to true or not present, the pod will be run in the host user namespace, useful
for when the pod needs a feature only available to the host user namespace, such as
loading a kernel module with CAP_SYS_MODULE.
When set to false, a new userns is created for the pod. Setting false is useful for
mitigating container breakout vulnerabilities even allowing users to run their
containers as root without actually having root privileges on the host.
This field is alpha-level and is only honored by servers that enable the UserNamespacesSupport feature.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>schedulingGates</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#podschedulinggate-v1-core"><code>[]PodSchedulingGate</code></a></td>
<td>

SchedulingGates is an opaque list of values that if specified will block scheduling the pod.
If schedulingGates is not empty, the pod will stay in the SchedulingGated state and the
scheduler will not attempt to schedule the pod.

SchedulingGates can only be set at pod creation time, and be removed only afterwards.


</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resourceClaims</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#podresourceclaim-v1-core"><code>[]PodResourceClaim</code></a></td>
<td>

ResourceClaims defines which ResourceClaims must be allocated
and reserved before the Pod is allowed to start. The resources
will be made available to those containers which consume them
by name.

This is an alpha field and requires enabling the
DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

This field is immutable.


</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RollingUpdate` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RollingUpdate}

Used by [`UpdateStrategy`](#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategy).

RollingUpdate paces rollout across Instances of one Component.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>partition</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Partition holds back updates for Instances whose index is &lt; Partition.
0 (the default) updates all Instances. Used for canary holds.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxUnavailable</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>
<td>

MaxUnavailable is the maximum number of Instances (or fraction) allowed
to be in a non-Ready state during the rollout. Accepts either an
absolute integer count (e.g. 2) or a percent string (e.g. &#34;25%&#34;).
Percent values resolve to ceil(replicas * percent / 100) at
reconcile time so the budget scales with the Component&#39;s replica count.
Unset inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value; when neither sets it and
the strategy is not SurgeThenDrain, the cluster default applies, and
without one this layer sets no cap.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxSurge</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>
<td>

MaxSurge is the maximum number of extra Instances (or fraction) the
rollout may create above the Component&#39;s desired replica count
during a rolling update. Accepts either an absolute integer count
(e.g. 1) or a percent string (e.g. &#34;25%&#34;). Percent values resolve
to ceil(replicas * percent / 100) at reconcile time. Mirrors the
semantics of upstream appsv1.Deployment.Strategy.RollingUpdate.MaxSurge
— extra capacity is created and brought to Ready before old Instances
are drained, enabling zero-capacity-dip rollouts.

When the Component participates in a RolloutCoordinationGroup with a
non-zero CoordinationPacing.MaxSurge, the group-wide ceiling caps the
per-Component MaxSurge. Unset inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value;
when neither sets it and the strategy is SurgeThenDrain, the cluster
default applies, and without one this layer sets no cap.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RolloutAnalysis` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutAnalysis}

Used by [`RolloutGroupStep`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroupStep).

RolloutAnalysis is a step&#39;s metric gate: the checks (metrics) and
policy (interval, failureLimit, onInconclusive, initialDelay) that decide
advance, hold, or rollback for the step it is set on. It does NOT carry the
metrics source — that is GroupCanary.Prometheus, shared by all analysis steps.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>interval</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Interval is the sampling cadence — how often the controller re-evaluates the
metrics while a step bakes. It also bounds the requeue while holding.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>initialDelay</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

InitialDelay is a warm-up after a step&#39;s pods become Ready and traffic is
applied, before the first sample. New pods need a moment before their metrics
mean anything; sampling immediately would read cold-start noise.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>failureLimit</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

FailureLimit is the number of failing samples, counted PER STEP (reset on
advance), that triggers auto-rollback. FailureLimit=1 rolls back on the first
bad sample.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>onInconclusive</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-OnInconclusive"><code>OnInconclusive</code></a></td>
<td>

OnInconclusive selects what to do when a sample cannot be completed
(Prometheus unreachable, query error, or empty result) past the stall
timeout — distinct from a metric breach.
  - Hold (default): keep traffic at the current step and escalate to Failed
    for an operator decision. A monitoring outage is not evidence the canary
    is bad.
  - Rollback: fail-safe — treat &#34;can&#39;t tell&#34; as &#34;assume bad&#34; and roll back
    on the first inconclusive sample, without waiting out the stall timeout.
  - RollbackOnStall: ride out transient gaps like Hold, but roll back
    instead of parking once the stall timeout expires.

Allowed values: `Hold`, `Rollback`, `RollbackOnStall`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>metrics</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-AnalysisMetric"><code>[]AnalysisMetric</code></a></td>
<td>

Metrics are the success conditions. A sample passes only when EVERY metric
passes (AND). At least one is required; an analysis with no metrics could
never fail and would gate nothing.

Minimum items: `1`. Maximum items: `10`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RolloutGroup` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup}

Used by [`RolloutRunGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRunGroup), [`RolloutSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutSpec).

RolloutGroup is a set of Components that roll together, advancing through at
most one progression. The progression is a presence-based one-of: set Canary,
BlueGreen, or RollingUpdate — or none, which defaults to BlueGreen. Omitting it
is the ergonomic spelling for &#34;just roll this group&#34; and for a single-Component
group in a sequence (`components: [decoder]` then `components: [engine]`),
where the empty `blueGreen: {}` selector would be pure ceremony.

Failure mode if mis-set: two progressions is ambiguous (which one drives
traffic?) and is rejected by the rule below.

Validation: at most one of canary, blueGreen, or rollingUpdate may be set on a rollout group.

Validation: order must reference only Components listed in this group.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>components</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentType"><code>[]ComponentType</code></a></td>
<td>

Components lists the Component names in this group (they roll together).
Valid values: &#34;router&#34;, &#34;engine&#34;, &#34;decoder&#34;.

Minimum items: `1`. Maximum items: `3`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>order</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ComponentType"><code>[]ComponentType</code></a></td>
<td>

Order optionally pins the sequence in which this group&#39;s Components roll.
No progression applies it — the Components in a group advance together —
so admission rejects a non-empty order (on create and on any update that
changes spec.rollout) rather than accept a sequence the engine does not
enforce. To roll Components one at a time, declare one single-Component
blueGreen group per Component, in the desired list order. Must reference
only Components in this group.

Maximum items: `3`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>canary</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupCanary"><code>GroupCanary</code></a></td>
<td>

Canary advances the group through explicit capacity + service-level-traffic
steps with optional gates. One-of progression.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>blueGreen</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupBlueGreen"><code>GroupBlueGreen</code></a></td>
<td>

BlueGreen surges the full new set, then flips traffic atomically. One-of
progression.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rollingUpdate</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupRollingUpdate"><code>GroupRollingUpdate</code></a></td>
<td>

RollingUpdate replaces pods gradually within the surge/unavailable budget,
tolerating mixed revisions during the window. One-of progression.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>policyRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPolicyRef"><code>RolloutPolicyRef</code></a></td>
<td>

PolicyRef names a same-namespace RolloutPolicy that supplies this
group&#39;s progression. A sibling of the progression one-of, not an arm of
it: the ref may coexist with one inline progression, and the inline
block wins (the preview/rollback mechanism) — the shadowed policy&#39;s
would-pin digest is published in status.rollout.groups[]. A group whose
only progression is an unresolvable ref PARKS at run open (fail-closed);
it never falls back to the default blueGreen, because silently removing
a declared gate is the failure this API exists to prevent.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>soak</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Soak is the wait AFTER this group completes, before the next group begins.
It is honored only when the rollout is a sequence of single-Component
blueGreen groups (the run that collapses to the internal Sequential state
machine); ignored on the last group. Admission rejects a soak the engine
would silently drop — on a canary, multi-Component, or rollingUpdate group,
or on a rollout that does not collapse to that sequence.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maintainRatio</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-MaintainRatio"><code>MaintainRatio</code></a></td>
<td>

MaintainRatio guards the cross-Component replica ratio while this group
rolls. Meaningful only on multi-Component blueGreen/rollingUpdate groups
(e.g. a PD engine+decoder pair); ignored on single-Component groups and
rejected by admission on canary groups (the canary engine does not enforce
it).

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<tr><td><code>index</code></td>

<td>

Index is the group&#39;s position in spec.rollout.groups[].

### `RolloutGroupStep` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroupStep}

Used by [`GroupCanary`](#ome-io-v1beta1-GroupCanary).

RolloutGroupStep is one stage of a canary progression. Capacity and traffic
are INDEPENDENT: capacity is the per-Component new-revision pod count; traffic
is the service-level percentage of requests on the new revision. The
independence allows &#34;capacity ahead of traffic&#34; (run 50% pods, send 10%
traffic) for warm-up.

How the step advances (its gate) is resolved in order:
  - Analysis set → metric-gated (queries GroupCanary.Prometheus); Pause.Duration,
    if any, is the minimum bake before a passing sample advances.
  - else Pause with Duration → timed: advance once Duration elapses.
  - else Pause → manual: hold for the ome.io/rollout-promote annotation.
  - else → advance as soon as capacity + traffic converge.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>capacity</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr#IntOrString"><code>IntOrString</code></a></td>
<td>

Capacity is the fraction of desired replicas to run on the new revision at
this step. Percentage (&#34;25%&#34;) or absolute (&#34;3&#34;). Per-Component.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>traffic</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Traffic is the service-level percentage of requests routed to the new
revision at this step (0-100). Not per-Component.

Minimum: `0`. Maximum: `100`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pause</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutPause"><code>RolloutPause</code></a></td>
<td>

Pause holds the step: with a Duration it is a timed advance (or, when
Analysis is set, the bake window); without one it is a manual hold for the
ome.io/rollout-promote annotation. Absent (and no Analysis) advances
immediately.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>analysis</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutAnalysis"><code>RolloutAnalysis</code></a></td>
<td>

Analysis opts this step into metric-gated promotion: it carries the checks
(metrics) and policy (interval, failureLimit, onInconclusive) for THIS step.
The metrics source is GroupCanary.Prometheus, shared by all analysis steps.
Absent leaves the step manual/timed/immediate per Pause.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RolloutHold` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutHold}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaStatus), [`LifecycleStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleStatus).

RolloutHold records the most recent reason a per-Instance Update was
denied for a Component — the detail behind &#34;why has this rollout not
moved&#34;. Overwritten whenever a reconcile observes a fresh denial;
cleared once the Component&#39;s rollout advances (an Update is admitted)
or completes (CurrentRevision == UpdateRevision, or no rollout is in
flight). Since is preserved across reconciles that keep reporting the
same Gate and Target, so it anchors &#34;held since&#34; rather than &#34;last
observed at&#34;.

<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>

<tr><td><code>gate</code></td>

<td>

Gate names the layer that produced Reason.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reason</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Reason is the operator-facing denial string from the gate that
produced it (e.g. &#34;Sequential waiting on decoder&#34;).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>target</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Target is the ControllerRevision name the held Update was aimed at.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>since</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

Since is when this Gate+Target combination was first observed
without interruption. A change in Gate or Target restarts the
clock; a change in Reason text alone does not (mirrors how
apimeta.SetStatusCondition preserves LastTransitionTime while a
condition&#39;s Status is unchanged).

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Used by [`RolloutGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup), [`RolloutGroupResolution`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroupResolution), [`RolloutRunGroup`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRunGroup), [`RolloutRunProvenance`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRunProvenance).

### `RolloutRun` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRun}

Used by [`RolloutStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutStatus).

<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>runID</code></td>

<td>

RunID uniquely names this run (stable for its lifetime; a retarget
closes the run and opens a new one with a new ID).

<td>

PinnedAt advances on every plan pin — the open, and each applied
repin. It is the run state&#39;s monotonic clock: concurrent status
writers keep whichever side is newer, so a reconcile working from a
stale cache can never roll a pinned plan back to a predecessor (a

(Superseded) and a fresh run opens with a fresh render.

</td></tr>

<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRunPlan"><code>RolloutRunPlan</code></a></td>

### `RolloutSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec).

RolloutSpec is the single rollout surface for an InferenceService: a list of
rollout groups. There is no coordination-vs-canary fork — canary is one
progression a group may choose, and whether list order sequences the groups
is GroupOrdering.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>groups</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroup"><code>[]RolloutGroup</code></a></td>
<td>

Groups is the ORDERED list of rollout groups. Sequence is the list
position: group N reaches completion before group N+1 begins. Components
listed together in one group roll together (a coupled unit); Components not
listed in any group roll independently (the default). To roll Components
one-at-a-time, put each in its own group, in order — a group needs only its
components; the progression may be omitted and defaults to blueGreen.

Cross-group sequencing is enforced only for a run of single-Component
blueGreen groups (the classic one-at-a-time shape). Under the default
groupOrdering: Sequential, admission rejects any other multi-group list —
a rollingUpdate, canary, or multi-Component group in an ordered list would
run concurrently, and an ordering the engine does not enforce is rejected
rather than accepted. The rejection applies on create and on any update
that changes spec.rollout, so stored objects keep reconciling until their
rollout is next edited. Set groupOrdering: Concurrent to declare that the
groups are independent and the list order promises nothing.

Only meaningful for OMENative-managed Components.

Maximum items: `3`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupOrdering</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutGroupOrdering"><code>RolloutGroupOrdering</code></a></td>
<td>

GroupOrdering declares what groups[] list order means. Sequential (the
default) promises group N completes before group N+1 begins, and is
admitted only for the shape that actually enforces it. Concurrent
declares the groups independent: they roll at the same time on their
disjoint Components, each with its own progression, gates, and
rollback. Concurrent is what lets one InferenceService run, say, a
router canary and an engine canary as unrelated rollouts.

Changing this does not change how the engine executes a list it could
not sequence — that was always concurrent. It changes whether such a
list is an error or a declaration of intent.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pairingProtocol</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PairingProtocol declares the engine↔decoder wire-compatibility contract
for prefill-decode pairing (e.g. a KV-transfer protocol generation, such
as &#34;nixl-v2&#34;). It is an opaque, operator-owned token compared only for
equality; bump it ONLY when the engine↔decoder wire contract breaks.
The value rides each engine and decoder revision: changing it mints new
revisions for both Components (a rollout), stamps ome.io/pairing-protocol
on their pods and per-revision Services, and is published on each traffic
target so routing pairs only engine and decoder revisions whose values
are equal. Empty or unset pairs with anything, so setting or clearing the
token is upgrade-neutral. Changing it between two non-empty values
requires engine and decoder to roll as one blueGreen or canary group.

Maximum length: `63`. Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9]([-A-Za-z0-9_.]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RolloutStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutStatus}

Used by [`InferenceServiceStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceStatus).

RolloutStatus is the run-model surface under status.rollout: the pinned
active run, a bounded record of the previous run, and the always-current
per-group resolution view (what WOULD pin now — the preview surface).

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>activeRun</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RolloutRun"><code>RolloutRun</code></a></td>
<td>

ActiveRun is the pinned plan the executors are consuming. Present iff a
run is open.

### `RoutingCapacitySpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingCapacitySpec}

Used by [`RoutingSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingSpec).

RoutingCapacitySpec configures polling each serving home for its current
servable capacity.

Validation: disabled must not be combined with capacity configuration fields.

Validation: an enabled capacity poll must specify path, method, format, period, timeout, samples, quorum, and maxAge.

Validation: period must be positive.

Validation: timeout must be positive.

Validation: timeout must be shorter than period.

Validation: maxAge must be at least period.

Validation: quorum must not exceed samples.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>disabled</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Disabled explicitly disables capacity polling. No other field may be set
when true.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Path is appended to each serving home&#39;s endpoint and must start with &#34;/&#34;.

Minimum length: `1`. Pattern: `^/`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>method</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Method is the HTTP method used by the capacity request.

Allowed values: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>format</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Format names the response shape returned by the capacity endpoint.

Minimum length: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>options</code></td>
<td><code>map[string]string</code></td>
<td>

Options contains format-specific settings interpreted by the configured
capacity format.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>period</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Period is how often each serving home is polled.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>timeout</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Timeout bounds one capacity request and must be shorter than Period.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>samples</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Samples is the number of recent readings in the capacity window.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>quorum</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Quorum is the number of readings required to corroborate a lower capacity.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxAge</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

MaxAge is the maximum accepted age of a capacity report.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `RoutingProbeSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingProbeSpec}

Used by [`RoutingSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingSpec).

RoutingProbeSpec configures an active end-to-end health probe for each
serving home&#39;s externally addressable endpoint.

Validation: disabled must not be combined with probe configuration fields.

Validation: an enabled probe must specify path, method, acceptStatuses, gateStatuses, period, timeout, failureThreshold, successThreshold, and allFailedPolicy.

Validation: period must be positive.

Validation: timeout must be positive.

Validation: timeout must be shorter than period.

Validation: gateStatuses must not contain 401, 403, or 429.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>disabled</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Disabled explicitly disables probing. No other field may be set when true.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Path is appended to each serving home&#39;s endpoint and must start with &#34;/&#34;.

Minimum length: `1`. Pattern: `^/`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>method</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Method is the HTTP method used by the probe.

Allowed values: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>acceptStatuses</code></td>
<td><code>[]int32</code></td>
<td>

AcceptStatuses are response codes counted as a successful probe.

Minimum items: `1`. Minimum per item: `100`. Maximum per item: `599`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>gateStatuses</code></td>
<td><code>[]int32</code></td>
<td>

GateStatuses are response codes counted as a failed probe. A code in
neither status list is inconclusive.

Minimum items: `1`. Maximum items: `500`. Minimum per item: `100`. Maximum per item: `599`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>period</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Period is how often each serving home is probed.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>timeout</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#duration-v1-meta"><code>Duration</code></a></td>
<td>

Timeout bounds one probe request and must be shorter than Period.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>failureThreshold</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

FailureThreshold is the number of consecutive failures required to gate a
serving home.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>successThreshold</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

SuccessThreshold is the number of consecutive successes required to
restore a gated serving home.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>allFailedPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RoutingAllFailedPolicy"><code>RoutingAllFailedPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

AllFailedPolicy controls the result when every serving home has crossed
the failure threshold.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `Runner` {#ome-io-v1beta1-Runner}

Used by [`InferenceReplicaSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceReplicaSpec).

Runner is one logical pod role within an Instance.

Single-pod Instances declare one Runner named &#34;default&#34; with Size=1.
Multi-node Instances declare &#34;leader&#34; (Size=1) + &#34;worker&#34; (Size&gt;=1).

The revision hash includes every Runner&#39;s Template; a worker-only
image bump still triggers a coordinated rollout across the whole
Instance because tensor-parallel weights require leader+workers to
move together.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>name</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RunnerName"><code>RunnerName</code></a></td>
<td>

Name is the Runner role within the Instance.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>size</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Size is the pod count for this Runner per Instance.
Constraints:
  - &#34;default&#34; Size MUST equal 1
  - &#34;leader&#34; Size MUST equal 1
  - &#34;worker&#34; Size MUST be &gt;= 1

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>template</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#podtemplatespec-v1-core"><code>PodTemplateSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Template is the fully-rendered pod template for this Runner.
Labels include ome.io/runner=&lt;name&gt;. The InferenceReplica
controller stamps OME_RUNNER (leader|worker|default) and,
for non-leader pods, OME_LEADER_ADDRESS (short-form DNS,
matching LWS conventions) onto the rendered pod at create.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Instance. Matches the established Runner vocabulary so existing
ome.io/runner label semantics carry through.

Allowed values: `default`, `leader`, `worker`.

### `SplitSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-SplitSpec}

Used by [`PlacementSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementSpec).

SplitSpec tunes how Split mode distributes replicas across candidate
clusters. All fields are optional and degrade to the documented defaults.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Replicas is the fleet-wide desired replica count to distribute across homes.
Unset falls back to the engine component&#39;s minReplicas (the guaranteed
floor) — the count OME actually guarantees running and thus the one worth
spreading. maxReplicas is deliberately NOT used (it is an autoscaling
ceiling that stays a per-home local concern).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spread</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Spread selects the apportionment policy. False (default) is Packed: fan out
in preference order and fill the fewest clusters the fleet&#39;s quota forces
(better locality, fewer endpoint backends). True is Balanced: apportion
~evenly (ceil(N/candidates)) so replicas spread across more clusters
(blast-radius resilience over locality).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>maxReplicasPerCluster</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

MaxReplicasPerCluster caps how many replicas one cluster may hold. It bounds
the over-request the fractional fan-out makes, and — combined with Spread —
is the lever that forces the fill to move on before a cluster is full
(deliberate spread without reading capacity). Zero means no cap.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>minReplicasPerCluster</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

MinReplicasPerCluster is the anti-sliver floor: a home that admits fewer
than this is dropped and its replicas returned to the deficit, so the
placement does not keep a home serving a tiny, uneconomical fraction. Zero
keeps any home that admitted &gt;=1.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `StorageSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-StorageSpec}

Used by [`BaseModelSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-BaseModelSpec), [`BenchmarkJobSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-BenchmarkJobSpec), [`FineTunedWeightSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-FineTunedWeightSpec).



<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Path is the absolute path where the model will be downloaded and stored on the node.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>schemaPath</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

SchemaPath is the path to the model schema or configuration file within the storage system.
This can be used to validate the model or customize how it&#39;s loaded.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>parameters</code></td>
<td><code>map[string]string</code></td>
<td>

Parameters contain key-value pairs to override default storage credentials or configuration.
These values are typically used to configure access to object storage or mount options.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>key</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Key is the name of a Secret that holds a Hugging Face token. The model
agent reads it only for hf:// models, from the model&#39;s namespace, or
from the ome namespace for a ClusterBaseModel. It takes the token from
the Secret&#39;s token key, or from the key that parameters.secretKey names.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storageUri</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

StorageUri specifies the source URI of the model in a supported storage backend.
Supported formats:

- OCI Object Storage:   oci://n/{namespace}/b/{bucket}/o/{object_path}
- Persistent Volume:    pvc://{pvc-name}/{sub-path}
- Vendor-specific:      vendor://{vendor-name}/{resource-type}/{resource-path}
- Hugging Face:         hf://{org}/{repo}[@{revision}]
- Amazon S3:            s3://{bucket}/{object_path}
- Azure Blob Storage:   az://{account}/{container}/{object_path}
- Google Cloud Storage: gs://{bucket}/{object_path}
- GitHub:               github://{org}/{repo}[@{tag}]
- Local filesystem:     local://{path}

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>nodeSelector</code></td>
<td><code>map[string]string</code></td>
<td>

NodeSelector defines a set of key-value label pairs that must be present on a node
for the model to be scheduled and downloaded onto that node.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>nodeAffinity</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#nodeaffinity-v1-core"><code>NodeAffinity</code></a></td>
<td>

NodeAffinity describes the node affinity rules that further constrain which nodes
are eligible to download and store this model, based on advanced scheduling policies.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>downloadPolicy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-DownloadPolicy"><code>DownloadPolicy</code></a></td>
<td>

DownloadPolicy describes the policy of downloading model artifacts.
Supported policies:

- AlwaysDownload, the default: always download a copy of the model to its path.
- ReuseIfExists: reuse Hugging Face files that another model already downloaded to the node.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
