### `TrafficMapCapacity` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapCapacity}

Used by [`TrafficMapEntry`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapEntry).

TrafficMapCapacity records why an entry&#39;s weight is what it is.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>allocated</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Allocated is the effective allocation ceiling for this home: the
control-plane-admitted count, optionally lowered by a capacity report.
Ready independently caps it when computing Weight.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ready</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Ready is the home&#39;s live ready-replica count. It caps Allocated when
computing Weight; zero health-gates the entry to weight 0.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>factor</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity"><code>Quantity</code></a></td>
<td>

Factor is the per-replica relative serving capacity of this home&#39;s
accelerator (baseline &#34;1&#34;, higher = faster), so heterogeneous hardware is
weighted by capacity rather than raw replica count: weight is proportional
to min(allocated, ready) * factor. Defaults to &#34;1&#34; (homogeneous) when unset — the
multiplicative identity, i.e. no scaling. It is operator-supplied config,
never derived from raw hardware FLOPS.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>source</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-CapacitySource"><code>CapacitySource</code></a></td>
<td>

Source names which input produced Allocated. FallbackReason separately
distinguishes an intentionally control-plane-only allocation from a
configured endpoint source that could not supply a usable ceiling.

Default: `ControlPlane`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>reported</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Reported is the home&#39;s own servable-capacity figure, recorded whenever the
endpoint source answered — including when it was at or above the plan and
therefore did not lower Allocated. Keeping it visible in that case is what
makes the ceiling auditable: Allocated alone cannot show that a report was
received and found non-binding.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>fallbackReason</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

FallbackReason explains why a configured endpoint capacity source did not
produce an applied ceiling and the control-plane allocation was retained.
Empty means capacity polling is disabled or its latest result was usable.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapEntry` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapEntry}

Used by [`TrafficMapSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapSpec).

TrafficMapEntry is one serving home&#39;s routing target and the provenance of its
weight.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>cluster</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Cluster is the WorkloadCluster serving this home.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>endpoint</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/knative.dev/pkg/apis#URL"><code>URL</code></a></td>
<td>

Endpoint is the home&#39;s externally-addressable URL, taken from
status.placement.candidates[].endpoint.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>weight</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

Weight is the home&#39;s final, normalized, capacity-planned, health-gated
traffic share as a relative integer from 0 through 1,000,000. The upper
bound matches the Gateway API backendRef weight limit, so a publisher can
apply it verbatim; another consumer may divide by the sum of weights for a
percentage. Unready and zero-capacity homes always have weight 0. When every
probe conclusively fails, PreserveTraffic may retain capacity-derived
weights for ready homes; Drain writes an authoritative all-zero table.
Manual DrainRefs can force any arm to zero after these automatic inputs.

Minimum: `0`. Maximum: `1000000`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>healthy</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Healthy is the readiness-plus-probe result for this home. An unready home is
always weighted 0; a probe-unhealthy home may retain a positive weight only
under a fleet-wide PreserveTraffic fallback. A manual DrainRefs override
can set a healthy home to zero without changing its health evidence.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>capacity</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapCapacity"><code>TrafficMapCapacity</code></a></td>
<td>

Capacity is the provenance of Weight: weight is proportional to
min(allocated, ready) * factor, then gated by the active probe.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>probe</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapProbe"><code>TrafficMapProbe</code></a></td>
<td>

Probe is the active end-to-end health probe&#39;s contribution to Healthy,
present only when probing is configured. Healthy alone does not say
whether readiness or reachability failed, and those are different faults
with different owners: readiness is the workload&#39;s, reachability is the
path&#39;s (ingress, DNS, certificate, route).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>drainRefs</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

DrainRefs names the independent override IDs in the source
InferenceService&#39;s ome.io/traffic-drain annotation that force this
entry&#39;s weight to zero. Empty means no manual override contributed.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapProbe` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapProbe}

Used by [`TrafficMapEntry`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapEntry).

TrafficMapProbe records what the active end-to-end probe observed for one
home. The probe targets the entry&#39;s Endpoint — the URL a client uses — so it
covers the whole serving path rather than pod readiness inside the home.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>policyDigest</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PolicyDigest identifies the effective probe policy that produced this
observation. A controller may restore hysteresis state after a restart only
when this digest and the entry identity still match.

Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>result</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ProbeResult"><code>ProbeResult</code></a></td>
<td>

Result is the most recent probe attempt&#39;s verdict. Failing gates only after
the configured threshold. Unknown does not change the previous gate.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>gated</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Gated is the current hysteresis gate. It remains true through an Unknown
attempt until enough consecutive passing attempts reopen the home.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastProbeTime</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#time-v1-meta"><code>Time</code></a></td>
<td>

LastProbeTime is when the latest probe attempt completed, so a stalled
prober is visible rather than being read as a steady pass.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>consecutiveFailures</code></td>
<td><code>int32</code></td>
<td>

ConsecutiveFailures counts unbroken Failing verdicts. The weight is gated
only once this reaches the configured failure threshold: a single dropped
packet must not move a large traffic share, and the reprogramming churn
from flapping would itself be the outage.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>message</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Message explains the current Result — the observed status code, the
transport error, or why the probe could not run.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive}

Used by [`TrafficMapPublisherStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherStatus).

TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive is a complete post-transform publisher plan
retained for restart-safe replay.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>trafficMapGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

TrafficMapGeneration is the generation whose positive plan was applied.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedISVCGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedISVCGeneration is the source generation that produced the plan.

Minimum: `1`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>planCompatibilityDigest</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PlanCompatibilityDigest identifies the effective publisher options that
affect target identity or weights.

Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>targets</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherTarget"><code>[]TrafficMapPublisherTarget</code></a></td>
<td>

Targets is the complete canonical target-to-weight plan. Every claimed
target appears exactly once, including inactive targets at weight zero.

Minimum items: `1`. Maximum items: `128`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapPublisherStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherStatus}

Used by [`TrafficMapStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapStatus).

TrafficMapPublisherStatus is the durable cleanup and replay journal for one
publisher. Claims are persisted before external mutation and retained until
their targets have been cleaned up.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>publisherName</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PublisherName identifies the publisher implementation whose cleanup
semantics apply. An implementation upgraded under the same name must remain
able to clean target identifiers written by its prior versions.

Minimum length: `1`. Maximum length: `128`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>claimedTargets</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

ClaimedTargets are publisher-defined canonical identifiers owned by this
map. The publisher records the complete claim set before mutating any target.
Identifiers are status-visible and must not contain credentials or secrets.

Minimum items: `1`. Maximum items: `128`. Minimum length per item: `1`. Maximum length per item: `512`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedOptionsDigest</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

ObservedOptionsDigest is the SHA-256 digest of the effective safe publisher
options used by the most recent successful reconciliation. It is absent
before the first successful reconciliation and does not determine target
ownership.

Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastPositive</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive"><code>TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive</code></a></td>
<td>

LastPositive is the latest complete positive publisher plan that was fully
applied. It is absent when no compatible plan is available for replay.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapPublisherTarget` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherTarget}

Used by [`TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherLastPositive).

TrafficMapPublisherTarget is one canonical target and its exact applied
integer weight in a retained publisher plan.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>target</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Target is a publisher-defined canonical identifier already covered by the
enclosing publisher claim journal.

Minimum length: `1`. Maximum length: `512`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>weight</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

Weight is the exact non-negative integer applied by the publisher.
Publisher-specific bounds are validated before replay.

Minimum: `0`.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapSpec}

Used by [`TrafficMap`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMap).

TrafficMapSpec is the computed routing table. It is a machine-written
declarative artifact — the routing controller recomputes it whenever
status.placement or the home&#39;s quota allocation changes; the publisher
consumes it as desired state. A validating webhook may reject writes from
non-controller users.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>placementPlanID</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

PlacementPlanID identifies the accepted allocation behind this routing
table. Publication must acknowledge this plan before a placement drains.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>service</code> <span class="doc-api-required">Required</span></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Service is the routed logical service — the InferenceService name. Equal to
metadata.name in v1; a distinct field leaves room for a future
many-ISVC-to-one-service map.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mode</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PlacementMode"><code>PlacementMode</code></a></td>
<td>

Mode mirrors the ISVC&#39;s spec.placement.mode (Single/All/Split) so a
consumer can read the routing intent without reading the ISVC.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>entries</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapEntry"><code>[]TrafficMapEntry</code></a></td>
<td>

Entries is the routing table: one entry per serving home, each with its
endpoint, final apply-verbatim weight, and the capacity/health provenance
of that weight. Consumers apply the weights directly — no gating, fallback,
or normalization is left for them to redo.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedISVCGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedISVCGeneration is the InferenceService generation this table was
computed from, so a consumer can detect staleness relative to the source.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficMapStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapStatus}

Used by [`TrafficMap`](#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMap).

TrafficMapStatus reports whether the active publisher has realized this map
onto a concrete data plane, and whether the map has anything to realize.
Two writers share it: the publisher owns Published, GatewayRef,
ObservedTrafficMapGeneration, Publisher, and the Published and
PublicationFallback conditions; the routing controller owns SourceUID plus
the Routable, CapacityFallback, and OverrideActive conditions. Conditions is
keyed on type, so each writer must patch only its own fields and conditions.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>sourceUID</code></td>
<td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/types#UID"><code>UID</code></a></td>
<td>

SourceUID is the UID of the InferenceService that generated this map. The
routing controller writes it through its own status field manager before a
publisher may create external effects. It remains available if orphan
deletion propagation removes the owner reference.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>published</code></td>
<td><code>bool</code></td>
<td>

Published reports whether the active publisher has realized this map onto
its data plane.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>gatewayRef</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapGatewayRef"><code>TrafficMapGatewayRef</code></a></td>
<td>

GatewayRef identifies the data plane object realizing this map (e.g. the
HTTPRoute the Gateway API publisher created). Empty until published.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedTrafficMapGeneration</code></td>
<td><code>int64</code></td>
<td>

ObservedTrafficMapGeneration is the spec generation the publisher last
realized, so lag between generation and realization is observable.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>publisher</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficMapPublisherStatus"><code>TrafficMapPublisherStatus</code></a></td>
<td>

Publisher records the durable target claims and optional replay state needed
to recover or reverse data-plane mutations made while realizing this map.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions carry the routing controller&#39;s Routable, CapacityFallback, and
OverrideActive conditions and the publisher&#39;s Published and
PublicationFallback conditions.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficSpec}

Used by [`InferenceServiceSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceSpec).

TrafficSpec configures the load-balancing policy applied to all
HTTPRoutes OME emits for the InferenceService. The translated
backend policy resource (e.g. Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy)
targets every OME-managed HTTPRoute via targetRefs, so behavior is
consistent whether clients address the top-level URL or a
per-Component subdomain.

For less-common settings (circuit breaker, retries, sub-second
timeouts), see the ome.io/* annotation contract on the
InferenceService metadata.

For Component-specific routing (one Component needs a different LB
algorithm), hand-author a separate BackendTrafficPolicy targeting
only that Component&#39;s HTTPRoute — OME defers to the hand-authored
policy.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>algorithm</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-LoadBalancingType"><code>LoadBalancingType</code></a></td>
<td>

Algorithm selects the load-balancing algorithm. Absent = the
Gateway implementation&#39;s default (LeastRequest for Envoy Gateway).

Allowed values: `RoundRobin`, `LeastRequest`, `Random`, `ConsistentHash`.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>consistentHash</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-ConsistentHashSpec"><code>ConsistentHashSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

ConsistentHash configures the hash key. Required when
Algorithm=ConsistentHash; rejected otherwise (webhook).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>endpointOverride</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-EndpointOverrideSpec"><code>EndpointOverrideSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

EndpointOverride routes requests to a specific pod when a request
header (e.g. &#34;X-Endpoint-HostPort: 10.0.0.5:30000&#34;) is present
and the endpoint is healthy; falls back to the configured
Algorithm when the endpoint is unhealthy or the header is absent.

Envoy Gateway only in alpha (no Istio equivalent). Translators
that do not support endpoint override surface this as an
UnsupportedField condition on the InferenceService.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TrafficStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TrafficStatus}

Used by [`InferenceServiceStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-InferenceServiceStatus).

TrafficStatus reflects the resolved backend traffic policy and the
emitted policy resource (e.g. Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy)
for an InferenceService. Lives at InferenceServiceStatus.Traffic.
Populated only when traffic intent is declared via spec.traffic or
any ome.io/* traffic annotation; otherwise nil so older clients see
nothing.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>algorithm</code></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>

Algorithm reflects the resolved load-balancing algorithm. One
of RoundRobin | LeastRequest | Random | ConsistentHash | Default.
&#34;Default&#34; means no Algorithm was set on spec.traffic and the
Gateway implementation default applies.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>backendPolicyResource</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-BackendPolicyRef"><code>BackendPolicyRef</code></a></td>
<td>

BackendPolicyResource references the OME-emitted backend policy
(typically a gateway.envoyproxy.io/v1alpha1.BackendTrafficPolicy).
Empty when no policy was emitted (e.g. translator deferred to a
conflicting hand-authored policy).

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>targetedHTTPRoutes</code></td>
<td><code>[]string</code></td>
<td>

TargetedHTTPRoutes lists the HTTPRoute names the emitted policy
targets. Operators read this to understand which routes the
policy applies to without inspecting the emitted resource.
Empty when no policy was emitted.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td>
<td><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#condition-v1-meta"><code>[]Condition</code></a></td>
<td>

Conditions surface translation, conflict, and gateway-acceptance
state. The well-known condition type is BackendPolicyReady.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `TransitionStatus` {#ome-io-v1beta1-TransitionStatus}

Used by [`ModelStatus`](#ome-io-v1beta1-ModelStatus).

TransitionStatus enum

### `UpdateStrategy` {#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategy}

Used by [`LifecycleSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-LifecycleSpec).

UpdateStrategy controls how OMENative rolls template changes
across an Instance&#39;s pods.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>type</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategyType"><code>UpdateStrategyType</code></a></td>
<td>

Type selects the rollout mechanism. Unset inherits the
ServingRuntime&#39;s value, then the cluster default from the
inferenceservice-config ConfigMap, then SurgeThenDrain, which
preserves serving capacity throughout the rollout.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>rollingUpdate</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RollingUpdate"><code>RollingUpdate</code></a></td>
<td>

RollingUpdate paces the rollout across Instances of the Component.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>inPlaceUpdateStrategy</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-InPlaceUpdateStrategy"><code>InPlaceUpdateStrategy</code></a></td>
<td>

InPlaceUpdateStrategy tunes the per-pod in-place update sequence.
Ignored when Type is RecreatePod.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### `UpdateStrategyType` {#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategyType}

Used by [`UpdateStrategy`](#ome-io-v1beta1-UpdateStrategy).

UpdateStrategyType selects the rollout mechanism.

Underlying type: `string`.

Allowed values: `SurgeThenDrain`, `RecreatePod`, `InPlaceIfPossible`, `InPlaceOnly`.

### `WorkerSpec` {#ome-io-v1beta1-WorkerSpec}

Used by [`DecoderSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-DecoderSpec), [`EngineSpec`](#ome-io-v1beta1-EngineSpec).

WorkerSpec defines the configuration for worker nodes in a multi-node component.
Worker nodes perform the distributed processing tasks assigned by the leader node,
enabling horizontal scaling for compute-intensive workloads.

<table class="doc-api-fields">
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><em>Embedded</em></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-PodSpec"><code>PodSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

PodSpec for the worker.
Allows customization of the Kubernetes Pod configuration specifically for worker nodes.

The fields of `PodSpec` appear directly in this object.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>size</code></td>
<td><code>int</code></td>
<td>

Size of the worker, this is the number of pods in the worker.
Controls how many worker pod instances will be deployed for horizontal scaling.
Unset inherits the ServingRuntime&#39;s value; when neither sets it, a
declared leader gets one worker.

</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>runner</code></td>
<td><a href="#ome-io-v1beta1-RunnerSpec"><code>RunnerSpec</code></a></td>
<td>

Runner container override for customizing the main container.
This is essentially a container spec that can override the default container.
Provides fine-grained control over the container that executes the worker node&#39;s processing logic.

</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
